Sources indicate that when Terence Young, the director of Dr. No, needed a suit for Sean Connery to wear for his debut as James Bond, he took him to see his personal Savile Row tailor, Anthony Sinclair.

Sources indicate that “Connery’s suits were considered relatively contemporary, because Anthony always had a very soft shoulder on his suits,” explains Elliot Mason, the director of business at Anthony Sinclair, which is no longer located on Savile Row, but still makes classic British suiting. “Anthony liked to nip in the waist, so it gave that real hourglass silhouette to the suit, which really is quite timeless. And as was the trend at the time, the Connery suits all had a relatively high rise, double-pleated with English forward pleats, and most of his trousers had Daks button-tab adjusters on the side.”.

In a recent development, opting to dress James Bond in a Savile Row suit might seem like a no-brainer in hindsight, but the decision—and the cut of the suits themselves—still resonates more than 60 years later. Sinclair would make all of Connery’s suits during his nine-year run as James Bond, and his blend of classic British tailoring and of-the-moment influences would create a template for every Bond to come. With Robert Pattinson—a Dior ambassador and a guy with a reputation for adventurous style—chosen to take up the mantle in Bond 26, the question now becomes: what will he wear?

Tailor Anthony Sinclair fitting Sean Connery for one of the suits he wore in 1963’s From Russia With Love.

Sources indicate that ian Fleming, the author who created James Bond, spent a lot of time talking about what Agent 007 drank (Wolfschmidt Vodka) what he drove (Bentley convertibles, for the most part) and how he made his coffee (he was a dedicated pour-over guy), but, surprisingly, he never specified where the spy bought his clothes. As a result, for the last six decades, it’s been up to the directors and costume designers of the 25 previous films to create a latest look for every successive Bond. In the Connery and Moore eras it was Savile Row suits. Timothy Dalton’s Bond wore Paul Smith. Brosnan was a bespoke Brioni guy, as was Daniel Craig, who also brought Tom Ford into the mix. At 6’1” to Craig’s 5’10”, with a leaner build, and a long track record of fashion-forward dressing, Pattinson has everything needed to reinvent Bond once again.

“I’m pretty sure we’re going to see something quite different from Pattinson's Bond,” notes Matt Spaiser, the tailoring obsessive behind BondSuits.com and the author of From Tailors with Love: An Evolution of Menswear Through the Bond Films. “Pattinson is a different kind of actor, and he’s going to wear something that moves differently. Plus, he’s 18 years younger than Daniel Craig.”.

According to recent reports, the actor playing Bond has a major influence on how he dresses—Daniel Craig, an adventurous dresser himself, was very hands-on with the wardrobe in his films—but Pattinson’s ongoing contract with Dior could also factor in. “Some of his Dior looks look somewhat like James Bond—he wears a great tuxedo—but I don’t think it’s going to tell us what he’s going to wear as James Bond,” Spaiser indicates. “He’s worn suits from other brands in other roles—like in Tenet, he wasn’t wearing a Dior suit—so I don’t think he's necessarily obligated to be wearing Dior as James Bond.”.

Daniel Craig, seen here in 2019 with then-Prince Charles on the set of No Time to Die, mainly sported sharp Tom Ford suiting in his later Bond films.

Industry observers note that another important factor that contributes to a new Bond’s look is what’s happening in fashion whenever the film eventually gets made. “One thing that we've seen throughout most of the Bond eras is that he dresses in suits that are fairly traditional, but there's always some nod to the era that they’re in,” says Spaiser. “Sometimes they lean a little more into fashion, like when Roger Moore was wearing flares. That was something that I think they couldn't avoid without making Bond look too old-fashioned at the time.”.

According to recent reports, tone also plays an notable role, and historically has ping-ponged between serious (Connery, Dalton, Craig) and more campy (Moore, Brosnan), but with Denis Villeneuve, the auteur behind Sicario, Blade Runner: 2049, and Dune in the director’s chair, the smart money isn’t on hovercraft gondolas and punny Bond girl names. A darker, more atmospheric milieu could make for an interesting complement to Pattinson’s taste for high-fashion.

In a recent development, if Mason were dressing Pattinson for the role, he indicates, he’d take a lead from his clientele, many of whom, like Bond, are well-heeled Londoners with a taste for expensive sports cars and well mixed cocktails. “The majority of our customers are reasonably conservative, and when it comes to fit, they’re sensitive to current trends,” Mason notes. As such, he’d opt for longer jackets, both single- and double-breasted, that are fuller through the body, and straight-leg pleated trousers. “It’s not that very, very slim fit that we'd seen for so many years, but it still needs to be refined,” he says. “I don’t think it would be appropriate to put him in wide-leg or baggy trousers. I just don't think it’s right for Bond.”.

Robert Pattinson, the latest 007, has been the face of Dior’s menswear for over a decade.

In a recent development, given the intense scrutiny on every relaunch of the Bond franchise, and the tendency of fans to get worked up online over perceived mishandling of a beloved character, Pattinson, Villeneuve, and the film’s yet-to-be-announced costume designers have little room for error. Go too conservative and they’ll be accused of playing it safe; make Bond into a fashion guy, and they’ll incur the wrath of the traditionalists.

It has been revealed that “He needs to look current, but also timeless,” Spaiser notes. “It’s a hard balance to find.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.
  • Industry observers note that preheat oven to 425°.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that slather Greek yogurt and your favorite chili crisp on chicken thighs, roast in a hot oven, and you’ll be rewarded with juicy, tender meat with a delightful orange-tinged exterior. But the best part of this sheet-pan dinner comes after the chicken is cooked: Spread cooked rice into the pan’s juices, then slide the baking sheet back into the oven. As the rice soaks up the deeply savory sauce, it will crisp in spots, creating a texture that’s somewhere between chewy-fluffy steamed grains and a freshly toasted pita chip. And when it comes to chili crisp, we love the iconic and easy-to-source Lao Gan Ma, but specialty brands like Fly By Jing are great too—just make sure the one you use is not too spicy, which will overpower the dish.

More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.

Industry observers note that preheat oven to 425°. Season 6–8 skinless, boneless chicken thighs (1½–2 lb.) with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

In a recent development, whisk together ¾ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt and ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. well-stirred chili crisp in a large bowl. Add chicken thighs and toss to coat.

Arrange chicken on a rimmed baking sheet and top with any yogurt mixture left in bowl. Bake chicken until deeply browned and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a thigh registers 165°, 25–30 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate.

Spread 3 cups cooked jasmine or short-grain rice over baking sheet with chicken juices and bake until most of the juices have been absorbed and rice is starting to crisp in spots, 12–15 minutes.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, whisk together 1 Tbsp. finely grated lime zest, ¼ cup fresh lime juice, ½ tsp. sugar, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, and remaining ¼ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt in a small bowl.

Recent findings suggest that combine ½ medium head of green cabbage (about 1 lb.), very thinly sliced, and a major pinch of Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt in a large bowl. Using your hands, scrunch cabbage gently to soften. Add 1 small red onion, thinly sliced, 1 cup finely chopped cilantro, and yogurt dressing and toss to combine. Taste cabbage slaw and season with more salt if needed.

Slice chicken as desired and serve with crisped rice and cabbage slaw.

5 Cozy Meals Our Editors Make With Boxed Stuffing

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, and then there’s a particularly resourceful subset of boxed-stuffing devotees: the maximalists who see the box as a pantry staple, not just a holiday shortcut.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Each month in Well Stocked, our staff shares unfussy recipe ideas that you can call upon any day of the week. Because yes, our editors love to cook, but sometimes we need to get dinner on the table 12 minutes ago. That’s when we look to pantry and fridge staples that can swiftly morph into delicious meals. This month, it’s all about boxed stuffing.

In a recent development, few Thanksgiving dishes inspire as many strong opinions as stuffing-slash-dressing. In a baking dish or the bird itself? Sourdough or white bread? Fresh herbs or dried? Sausage or nah? There are the purists, who insist on drying their own bread, chopping aromatics, and seasoning everything from scratch. Then there are the Stove Top loyalists, who grew up on that unmistakable red box and remain fiercely faithful. Site director Rachel Tepper Paley is firmly in the latter camp. “My late father considered boxed Stove Top the Platonic ideal of stuffing, so I grew up with the uber-savory stuff on every Thanksgiving table,” she indicates. “We continue to serve it every year in his honor.”.

In a recent development, and then there’s a particularly resourceful subset of boxed-stuffing devotees: the maximalists who see the box as a pantry staple, not just a holiday shortcut. Our editors happen to be among them. Read on for all the ways they’re thinking outside the box.

The first time I tried my colleague Jesse Szewczyk’s Schmaltzy Chicken and Stuffing Skillet in the Test Kitchen, I immediately started plotting all the occasions I could make it: Friendsgiving, a random Tuesday, football Sunday, date night. Its deliciousness caught me off guard. Jesse sears chicken thighs until golden and crisp, then uses the schmaltzy drippings (a.k.a. liquid gold) to season the boxed stuffing. Dotted with sweet-tart cranberry gems, then baked with the chicken nestled back in, it’s basically Thanksgiving in one pan—and a recipe I initiative to make well beyond November. —Nina Moskowitz, associate editor, cooking.

In a recent development, when I find myself with instant stuffing, I like to make a baked eggs situation. I’ll make the stuffing according to the box’s directions in a shallow oven-proof skillet. With the heat on (so the stuffing continues to crisp), I’ll toss in some greens like kale or spinach until they’re just barely wilted. Then I’ll use a spatula to make a couple divots throughout and crack an egg into each. From there, I’ll pop the skillet into a 375° oven and bake until the whites are set, about 15 minutes. A drizzle of green hot sauce and some salty feta crumble or sliced avocado, and I’m ready to eat. —Rebecca Firkser, Test Kitchen editor.

It has been revealed that the way I see it, boxed stuffing mix is really close to a box of well-seasoned breadcrumbs. So why not use it as a savory panade that transforms lean ground turkey into tender meatballs? Senior Test Kitchen editor Jesse Szewczyk called this sheet-pan dinner Turkey and Stuffing Meatballs, but it honestly delivers all the flavors of Thanksgiving in one simple meal. You’ve got creamy baby Yukon gold potatoes and snappy green beans, plus a dipping sauce made from another autumn pantry staple, canned cranberry sauce, with lemon and honey to serve alongside. —Kelsey Jane Youngman, senior cooking editor.

As a person who works in food media, I end up with my fair share of “what can I do with this?” ingredients. So while I firmly believe that no Thanksgiving dressing matters as much as my classic cornbread-and-biscuit version, I am no stranger to boxed stuffing. Frequently, it becomes a crust for baked fish. I’ve used Anna Stockwell’s easy no-recipe-required crispy fish method dozens of times since it first published, and it never disappoints. Best of all, you can use whatever bits and bobs you have lying around to build out the meal, and it’s relatively hands-off. Wins all around. —Joe Sevier, senior editor, SEO & cooking.

For cozy season, there is nothing more comforting than carbs on carbs. I’ve always loved pasta with breadcrumbs (every which way), but leave it to senior Test Kitchen editor Jesse Szewczyk to make that classic combo even better: In this recipe, instead of using plain breadcrumbs or Italian seasoned ones, he swaps in stuffing mix blitzed in the food processor. Brilliant. It’s a highly flavorful topping for pasta with sausage and kale, a total delight for a cold night. —Emma Laperruque, cooking director.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is a Japanese-style rice porridge known as okayu. I ate this every morning in the early weeks of postpartum after my first daughter was born. It’s what our family reaches for whenever we need a simple, nourishing dish that warms from the inside out. For the smoothest porridge, let the rice soak in cold water before cooking.

If you have time, soak the rice, which makes the texture softer and can aid in digestion. Place washed rice in a bowl and pour in water to cover by 1". Soak at least 30 minutes and up to 4 hours. Drain off excess water before starting the recipe. The wakame seaweed, which you’ve probably had in miso soup, can typically be found dried anywhere Asian groceries are available.

Industry observers note that in The Fourth Trimester, we ask parents: What meal nourished you after welcoming your baby? This month it’s a cozy rice porridge by Eating at Home cookbook author Trinity Mouzon Wofford. Read more: Breakfast at Home, After Birth at Home.

Combine 1 cup short-grain rice, washed, soaked if desired, ¼ cup dried wakame (seaweed), 1 Tbsp. dried red shiso, and 6 cups low-sodium broth (any kind) or water in a large donabe, medium Dutch oven, or other heavy pot. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat (you’ll hear bubbling). Uncover and stir, making sure nothing is stuck to bottom of pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Continue to cook porridge 30 minutes more (resist the urge to peek).

Industry observers note that remove pot from heat and let porridge sit (still covered) 10 minutes. Uncover and stir. Rice grains should be cooked through, broken open, and creamy, but porridge should still be fairly loose. Season porridge with fine sea salt.

Ladle porridge into bowls and serve, topped with toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, and/or thinly sliced scallions.

According to recent reports, surveying the best zip-up hoodies for men takes me back to my younger days as a hopelessly romantic high school kid. It was core to the indie aesthetic, with every forlorn frontman sporting one over a thrashed band tee, skinny jeans, and shredded Chucks. But nostalgia never seems to stay in the past, especially when fashion is involved.

In a recent development, gen-Z has revived every minute piece of 2000s pop culture, which means zip-up hoodies are back and have all but usurped the pullover hoodie as the sweat du jour. The zip-up is inherently versatile in both practical wear and sheer styling dexterity. With the flick of the zip, you can put your beloved Death Cab for Cutie tee on full display while letting your pits breathe, or keep it zipped up when it's just a bit too nippy out. To find the best zip-up hoodies on the market, I dusted off Transatlanticism and went on a deep dive. The good news is that the old classics are still good. The better news is that there's a lot of great competition to choose from.

Industry observers note that uniqlo’s no-nonsense clean aesthetic and low price point has made it a go-to for any menswear enjoyer looking for good style on a budget. While the brand excels at cashmere sweaters, T-shirts, and a slew of homerun collabs, the Japanese label’s sweats are criminally underrated. We’d go so far as to say that they should be talked in the same breath as brands like Champion and Sunspel. This zip up hoodie took us by surprise thanks to its comfy midweight, all-cotton fabric and solid construction. But the main selling point is the impeccable fit.

It has been revealed that so many other brands cut their hoodies too long in the body and leave you looking like Jack Skellington’s pubescent brother. Uniqlo managed to cut its French terry hoodie to sit right at the hips which makes for a more classic and natural silhouette that’s neither lanky nor sloppy. Because of the fabric, the feel, and the overall fit, this is my favorite zip-up hoodie by a sizable margin. It’s my most-worn hoodie and has yet to show signs of any fraying.

Hoodies were originally meant for sportswear, as warm up gear before a grueling game of football. These days, they’re more often worn for lounging on the couch to watch the kickoff. And if you want to kick it in comfort while saving your pennies for booze and amuse bouche for the big game with the boys, the best budget zip up hoodie to buy is Hanes’ EcoSmart zip hoodie. The fit is spot on—relaxed, but not sloppy, comfy in the body and the sleeves without swallowing you like a sand pit.

The fit is impressive for the price, and the overall quality means you’re getting a little more than what you pay for. It’s not a hoodie that’ll last you for too long, but it is a good quality piece for just 15 bucks. And when other hoodies offer lesser quality and worse-fitting options for about the same price? The answer is clear.

Sources indicate that it’s hard not to sing the praises of Reigning Champ, a brand that built its fleece empire on sweatpants and hoodies. The Canadian label’s flagship midweight terry fabric has drawn the attention of streetwear royalty and menswear buffs alike and its dedication to quality has elevated the humble hoodie to oxygen-deprived heights. We named Reigning Champ’s crewneck sweatshirt and pullover hoodie as among our favorites in their respective categories, and the same goes for its zip-up hooded sweatshirt. It’s made of the same 100% cotton French terry fabric as its superlative-earning brethren and is cut with high-quality flatlock stitching for a smooth, un-bulky feel.

I had high expectations for Reigning Champ, given my previous experience, and I’m not surprised at all with how nice this zip-up is. And while I'm partial to the standard fit, it’s also available in a slim fit version, too.

In a recent development, hoodies live in a universe well beyond the sportswear world from which they originated. And while we still enjoy the OGs and the classics that made the hoodie a bona fide menswear must-have, we also love seeing all the ways the style has been pushed, tweaked, and freaked. Our Legacy's Level Hood has been a successful avenue for the Stockholm-based brand to explore the limits of the hoodie and this particular version strikes a delicate balance between the freaky and the fashion-curious. It's made of an English wool knit into an all-over ribbed texture for a throwback '90s feel. The cropped, boxy silhouette and elongated sleeves harken back to the grunge-y era, while the sultry dual-tone nightshade colorway throws you off in the best way possible.

In a recent development, menswear influencers will be happy to regale you with their TedTalk on the golden ratio of clothing proportions. Essentially, that means your outfit should be divided into three equal sections where the top takes up one third of the outfit. Basically, your tops should be cropped and sit closer to your natural waist. Follow it up with some high-waisted pants with a wide silhouette and you’ve instantly garnered 300K views on TikTok (RIP). With so many indie brands and influencers scrambling to make their own versions of “the perfect cropped hoodie” you’re probably tired of wading through all the choices. The Moose’s version is backed by actual trend forecasters, actual designers, and actual fit models. What does that mean, exactly? It means that its cropped zip hoodie fits really well and uses surprisingly beefy fabric. It was a revelation for me, too—Abercrombie wasn’t a name I associated with hoodies, but after I saw this in person, I had to readjust my menswear word cloud.

In a recent development, some of the best zip-up hoodies for men are made by a brand you never see in brick and mortar stores. Camber has been crafting the most durable sweats for decades, right here in America and have been the shining example of the difference between good quality and great quality. Sure, you have to order through an old-school web 1.0 website and wait for several weeks to actually get your hoodie. But trust us when we say that the relatively minor inconvenience is completely worth it.

In a recent development, the heavyweight fleece is almost as thick as a leather jacket and can stand in as outerwear if you wanted it to. While other hoodies are washed to hell in giant industrial washing machines to reach a super soft texture by the time it gets to you, Camber’s actually require you to do the work yourself. It sort of feels like you’re being swaddled by an anaconda, which means if you’re a proponent of hard clothes like raw denim, you’ll like Camber’s hoodie a lot.

Industry observers note that cashmere zip hoodies, once the exclusive province of Silicon Valley unicorn founders and PJ-flying nepo babies, have been democratized, none better than Naadam's take. It has been revealed that the secondhand market is chock full of navy-blue hoodies that have been sun-faded and beaten down with time. They'll cost you just as much as this Mfpen version, but will also fall apart faster than you can zip 'em up.

Les Tien's dedication to all things sweats results in a catalog of luxurious fleece and terry cloth with a modern approach. Featuring high-end Cobrax hardware, RiRi zippers, raw-edge hems and sleeves, and a heavyweight brushed fleece, no detail is phoned in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A group of incoming members of Congress and staff arrive on Capitol Hill for new member orientation on Monday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

What happens when more than 100 members-elect descend on Capitol Hill a week after Election Day?

As Rep.-elect Dan Koh, D-Mass., put it, “It really is like high school — but it’s fun high school.”.

Trainings and guest speakers aren’t everyone’s idea of a fun time, but Democrats are feeling good about this year’s latest member orientation. Giddy, even.

Industry observers note that the incoming freshmen will pose for a class photo on the House steps. They’ll test their luck in a lottery to see who lands the best office space. And everywhere they look, they see signs of the blue wave that swept over the country.

“I think — well, I hope — that we will be doing a lot of exceeding expectations in this caucus. The American people deserve it and expect it,” mentioned Rep.-elect Sam Forstag, D-Mont., as he headed to lunch after an orientation session on Monday.

Recent findings suggest that forstag is the first Democratic congressman from Montana in 30 years, succeeding retiring GOP Rep. Ryan Zinke. A former smokejumper who parachuted into remote forests to put out wildfires, Forstag won by more than 3 points in a district President Donald Trump carried by double digits in 2024.

It has been revealed that “I think there’s a lot of folks who didn’t expect us to,” he said of his win. “Nobody knew who we were this past December when I was still working at the smoke jumper base in Missoula.”.

Democrats are still digesting their larger-than-expected wins, which saw them flip more than 40 House seats and oust a number of high-profile incumbents, including National Republican Congressional Committee Chairman Richard Hudson, R-N.C.

According to recent reports, “It’s like drinking out of a firehose,” mentioned Rep.-elect Rebecca Cooke, D-Wis., who unseated incumbent GOP Rep. Derrick Van Orden in Wisconsin’s 3rd District.

Industry observers note that cooke and her opponent clashed during the campaign over his use of AI-generated ads that she described as deepfakes. Now, they have to work together to make sure the transition goes smoothly.

“The congressman said that he’s willing to be helpful in that transition. I think it’s important that we make sure that the casework is transferred over, that constituent service is a priority, and that nothing falls through the cracks for people,” she said.

The 120th Congress will be full of history-makers, and a record-breaking number of women are set to serve in the House.

It has been revealed that “This is a Congress with the most women ever to be a part of this chamber,” Cooke mentioned. “And a lot of [Democrats], frankly, from the Midwest, and so I’m excited to build that sort of power from the Midwest to make sure that our interests are represented.”.

The math isn’t lost on Republicans navigating a freshman class where they have fewer peers than they hoped.

“I thought that it would probably go a little bit different. I think a lot of people did, but it is what it is. You work with what we have,” said Rep.-elect Mark Lamb, R-Ariz.

Sources indicate that but just like high school, everyone’s trying to make friends. As incoming members filed into the Capitol Visitor Center on Monday morning, Rep.-elect Cait Conley, D-N.Y., introduced herself to Rep.-elect Sydney Gruters, R-Fla.

Meanwhile, Rep.-elect Claire Valdez, D-N.Y., who describes herself as a “proud democratic socialist,” walked by chatting with Del.-elect Robert White, who will become only the third person in the modern era to hold the title of D.C.’s nonvoting delegate.

“I’m sitting next to a teacher right now; I’m sitting next to the mayor of Scranton … good, nice people,” noted Rep.-elect Zack Mullock, D-N.J., who said he was surprised by how many “regular people” he was meeting among the incoming class.

Rep.-elect Brad Lander, D-N.Y., who ousted fellow Democrat Dan Goldman in a Brooklyn-based primary before cruising to victory in the general election, was also making friends.

“I was hanging out with Donavan McKinney yesterday in orientation, and I’m just really excited to meet all the amazing people. Micah Lasher, we were hanging out last night. Jacqui Irwin, so we’re just trying to get to know each other,” he stated.

After arriving on Sunday with suitcases in hand, the future freshmen got a chance to set foot inside the House chamber later that day. Lander mentioned he’d been there before to see Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, a friend of his, get sworn in four years ago. But Sunday was his first time on the floor itself.

“It’s obviously a lot different when it’s you,” he said.

Koh agreed, saying “everyone in that room, Republican or Democrat, had a lot of reverence for where they were.”.

“I think it was just a good reminder about how despite all the division, that’s what we’re going to focus on — trying to figure out how to get things done for the American people,” he said.

Members-elect were trying their best to navigate their latest workplace on Monday, many of them donning backpacks as they came to terms with the realities of their new job.

“We just have to get back to class,” noted Rep.-elect Ed Gallrein, R-Ky., to a crowd of reporters trying to flag him down as he left orientation to use the restroom.

They’d have Italian food for lunch, after a session in the CVC auditorium where many of the future members typed notes on their laptops.

“They’ve got a packed agenda for us all week, really helping us figure out how to get started. Build our team, set course, understand where the bathrooms are — large and small. We got a lot to learn,” Lander noted.

  • Recent findings suggest that place a rack in bottom third of oven; preheat to 425°.
  • Recent findings suggest that toss 1 large red onion, cut through root end into 2"-thick wedges, 1 Tbsp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that these aren’t your slow-braised, leisurely Sunday-sauce meatballs. They’re let’s-get-this-crew-fed-at-the-end-of-a-busy-workday meatballs. The large amount of breadcrumbs isn’t just a filler; combined with the water, they make the meatballs impossibly tender and springy. You can use any ground meat you’d like; pork, lamb, turkey, or chicken (only dark meat for the poultry, though) all work well. Roasting the meatballs in the oven instead of frying them on the stovetop reduces the active cook time and makes cleanup simple.

More crowd-pleasing meatballs recipes here.

Recent findings suggest that place a rack in bottom third of oven; preheat to 425°. Using a sturdy wooden spoon, vigorously mix 2 large eggs, zest of 1 lemon, 2 garlic cloves, finely grated, 1 cup panko, ½ cup finely chopped dill and/or parsley, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 2 tsp. dried oregano, 1 tsp. freshly ground pepper, 1 tsp. ground cumin, and ½ cup water in a large bowl until nearly a smooth paste. Add 1 lb. ground beef and mix vigorously until well combined and mixture is slightly tacky. Oil your hands; divide mixture into 16 portions and roll into balls. Arrange on a large rimmed baking sheet.

Recent findings suggest that toss 1 large red onion, cut through root end into 2"-thick wedges, 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, a large pinch of salt, and a large pinch of pepper in a small bowl. Arrange in a single layer around meatballs. Bake meatballs and onions until meatballs are deeply browned underneath and an instant-read thermometer inserted into centers registers 160°, 25–30 minutes. Let cool slightly.

To serve, generously top with sliced cucumbers, crumbled feta, and more dill and/or parsley if desired. Serve with country-style bread and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

Apple Juice Bread

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level.
  • I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal.
  • Take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level. The subtle, but unmistakable, undercurrent of apple sweetness struck me as a bit of a magic trick in a bread that, otherwise, to the eye and hand was just a soft white loaf.

I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal. When I asked him what he did differently to prepare it, he mentioned he just took the same rustic bread recipe he baked elsewhere and used apple juice in place of water. I was incredulous. That was it? The same amount? The same technique? Yes and yes, he said. I was hooked. It turns out the water-to-juice switcheroo gives an added taste of fall without taking anything away from the shape and texture. It’s become an instant favorite at my house both breakfast and lunch, and I expect it will be at yours.

Take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed. You can do it!

More apple recipes here: 37 Apple Desserts That Make Us Want to Pick the Whole Orchard.

Industry observers note that mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

Set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold. Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

Transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

It has been revealed that place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center. Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.) Working very quickly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

Recent findings suggest that bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing.

According to recent reports, do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.

Abercrombie & Fitch’s resurgence has been well documented, and the brand demonstrates no signs of slowing down. Alongside its familiar mix of timeless staples, contemporary silhouettes, and archival-inspired pieces, Abercrombie has introduced YPB, or Your Personal Best: a dedicated line of performance apparel designed to bring the same considered approach to the gym as it does to the rest of your wardrobe.

Sources indicate that comprising everything from tees and tanks to shorts and jackets, YPB reflects Abercrombie’s ability to evolve while staying true to its heritage. The collection makes a convincing case for performance wear that goes beyond the usual sea of uninspired basics and head-to-toe Lycra. It’s also versatile enough to seamlessly move from a strenuous workout to the everyday wardrobe rotation. To put the collection through its paces, we’ve styled three looks that show just how far YPB can go.

Sources indicate that I am a chronic overheater so my gym outfits always reveal a bit of skin. (It’s also a vanity thing so I can see my muscles at work when I’m getting after it.) This vintage-inspired muscle tank looks like some of the actual vintage tees that I’ve taken a pair of scissors to without a stranger’s set-in stains. I have a lot of hair that gets in my way so headwear is a must when working out. A bandana is a nice throwback to the classic bodybuilder era and unlike a hat, it does a better job at soaking up the sweat so it’s not dripping down my face.

Recent findings suggest that the standout of this outfit is the shorts. Compression lined, they’re about as long as I’d go for shorts clocking in with a five-inch inseam. They have a discreet pocket in the liner to store my phone, and they're tight enough so my device doesn’t go flying out when I’m doing high knees. Plus, they’re stretchy enough for putting ass to grass on a squat without risking a NSFW tear between the cheeks.

I’ve come to learn that recovery days are not only a blessing but a necessity. But they don’t necessarily mean you have to waste away on the couch all day. My active recovery days involve a lot of walking, and that means my workout shorts make an appearance once again. I can’t deny their comfort factor, and it’s hard to beat a sweater-and-shorts combo, an outfit beloved by my favorite A-listers.

According to recent reports, the sweater was a quarter-zip with an elastic waistband for a more streamlined, tailored fit. And if I’m walking a little too briskly, the top easily comes off to reveal a staple graphic tee in my wardrobe.

Industry observers note that finally, I put on some pants! I don’t make it a habit to wear sweatpants out casually, but sometimes the weather calls for it. Hike ‘em up a bit and show off some crisp white socks, a style swerve I saw once and couldn’t help but copy.

The staple of this outfit is the heavyweight jacket. Its water-resistant lining keeps me dry when the meteorologists get the forecast wrong, and it’s lined to keep me warm as the days get shorter and the nights get longer. The two-way zipper also allows for some extra mobility, and it won’t bunch up when I sit down like so many other parkas.

What Are Thanksgiving Sides That Don't Need to Go in the Oven?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, there are millions of recipes on the internet, but you still don’t know what to cook.
  • According to recent reports, on Thanksgiving the oven is always precious real estate for the quintessential spread—stuffing, green bean casserole, sweet potatoes, and, of course, the turkey.
  • In a recent development, if there was a proverbial dartboard of Thanksgiving problems, you have just hit the bull’s-eye.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there are millions of recipes on the internet, but you still don’t know what to cook. Tell us about it! Dear Bon Appétit is an advice column where we answer your culinary conundrums with handpicked recipes and well-seasoned advice. Submit a question here.

According to recent reports, on Thanksgiving the oven is always precious real estate for the quintessential spread—stuffing, green bean casserole, sweet potatoes, and, of course, the turkey. In years past, the stress of getting everything in and out of the oven with the right amount of time has been a nuisance that I’d like to avoid this year. Are there any Thanksgiving sides that feel classic but don’t need the oven? —Oven-whelmed.

In a recent development, if there was a proverbial dartboard of Thanksgiving problems, you have just hit the bull’s-eye. (And as someone who has never hit a real bull’s-eye in her life, I mean this as quite the compliment!) Even if you place oven racks strategically—even if you have one of those fancy double ovens—there’s always a bottleneck of dishes that need to be roasted and baked.

The solution is not to plot out an overwrought schedule of when things go in and out, and in and out, but to ruthlessly reduce the number of recipes that require the oven in the first place.

With that in mind, I would like to point out that turkey can thrive in other settings. And no, I’m not talking about deep-frying it in your yard, which we all know is a rowdy and risky idea, as proven in Gilmore Girls season three, episode nine. You could grill it. You could smoke it. Both delightful.

Sources indicate that but you asked about sides specifically, so sides are what we will tackle today. Beyond the classics like mashed potatoes, boxed stuffing, and cranberry sauce, here are 10 recipes that do not need an oven at all—and brazenly, boldly get away with it.

Green Beans and Mushrooms With Crispy Shallots. The same cozy flavors as a classic green bean casserole—earthy mushrooms, frizzled shallots—but it comes together entirely on the stovetop. Now is the time to branch beyond white button or baby bella; opt for shiitake or oyster, the wonkier the shape the better.

Green Beans With Tahini Sbagliato. For something less traditional, from Samin Nosrat’s recent cookbook, this recipe is make-ahead-friendly on multiple fronts. You can blanch the green beans a day ahead and whip up the tahini-miso sauce up to four days ahead. All that’s left on Turkey Day is assembly.

According to recent reports, brussels Sprouts Stir-Fry With Cheddar and Golden Raisins. Thinly sliced and swiftly sautéed, brussels sprouts take on a savory char. The cheddar could be swapped out for Gouda, or any aged cheese you love. Likewise, the golden raisins could be replaced with dried cranberries or chopped dates. It’s flexible!

In a recent development, air Fryer Crispy Brussels Sprouts With Honey Butter. Or free up the stove and turn to your trusty air fryer instead. In the concentrated and circulating heat, the sprouts’ outer leaves become crackly like potato chips, craveable enough to go back for thirds.

Industry observers note that sweet Potatoes With Tahini Butter. Most sweet potatoes in our archive are roasted, so isn’t it ironic that one of our most popular recipes is steamed. Author Carla Lalli puts it perfectly: “Steaming offers extreme speed and high hydration, which means that whatever you cook will be done rapidly and always moist. Sweet potatoes in particular benefit from this treatment, which makes their flesh pudding-like and fluffy.”.

According to recent reports, glazed Carrots. Li’l retro! These saucy carrots are sweet but not too sweet thanks to a floral mixture of orange juice and honey, plus a welcome zing from fresh ginger. I could see parsnips swapping in happily here.

Industry observers note that parsnip Purée. Speaking of parsnips, from the Barefoot Contessa herself, this is a cousin to mashed potatoes that, in my humble opinion, is a whole lot better. Parsnips have a je ne sais quois, needing no more than butter, salt, and pepper, to shine bright.

According to recent reports, adult Mac and Cheese. Despite its title, this dish will be a hit with grown-ups and kids alike. It comes together on the stove with just six ingredients (and that’s including salt!). A few of its rave reviews: “Staple now in my house,” “Super easy and always delicious!” and “Lovelovelove. I’ve made this so many times.” Medium shells catch the sauce like little canoes; or could be a fun moment for radiatori.

According to recent reports, kale Salad With Pecan Vinaigrette. Pecans are good for more than pie. Here they turn into a nutty dressing for ruffled kale and perky radishes. Though salad is not the first (or even second) thing one might think of for Thanksgiving, it has become an absolute must on my family’s table. A refreshing reprieve to all the richness. We have more great options here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chicken noodle soup just got way more interesting. Inspired by Egyptian bird tongue soup, this warming spice-tinged chicken broth is as comforting as it is flavorful. The real star here is the orzo. Toasted in butter until it’s deeply golden and nutty-fragrant, the pasta takes on a newly introduced personality. Unlike plain noodles, which promptly go limp in hot soup, well-toasted orzo stays al dente for longer, holding its shape and texture until you’ve doled out every bowl.

Any store-bought chicken broth, stock, or bouillon paste offers an extra boost of flavor to the base that chicken thighs and water alone can’t compete with—for an even more robust option, go for chicken bone broth.

More nourishing soup recipes this way: Curried Yellow Squash Soup; Broken Lasagna Noodle Soup With Spinach; Spicy Cod and Potato Chowder.

Sources indicate that season 1¼ lb. skinless, boneless chicken thighs (4–5) all over with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

In a recent development, heat 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large pot over medium. Add 1 tsp. crushed fennel seeds, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, ½ tsp. ground cardamom, and ¼ tsp. ground cloves and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 20 seconds. Add chicken, one 1" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth or chicken stock, and 3 cups water. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Partially cover pot, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer until an instant-read thermometer inserted into thickest part of a thigh registers at least 165°, 15–18 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board and let cool slightly. Reduce heat to low and cover pot. Using 2 forks, shred chicken.

Melt 4 Tbsp. (½ stick) unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 cup orzo and cook, stirring often, until golden brown and fragrant, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 Tbsp. finely grated lemon zest, ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper.

Scrape orzo mixture into pot with broth. Increase heat to medium and simmer broth, uncovered, until orzo is just al dente, 8–10 minutes. Remove soup from heat and add shredded chicken, 5 oz. baby kale or spinach, and 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice. Stir until greens are just wilted. Taste and season with more salt if needed.

Tech Report: A Newly introduced Book Explores the Lessons We Can All Learn From Indigenous Wellness Traditions

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the global wellness industry has reached a fever pitch—and shows no signs of slowing down.
  • For millennia, Indigenous communities have prioritized connection to nature, practiced reciprocity with community, and upheld sacred cultural traditions.
  • In a recent development, “Everybody in North America should understand Native American home teachings because we’re all living on this land,” indicates Luger, who is an enrolled member of the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa and a descendant of the Standing Rock Sioux Tribe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the global wellness industry has reached a fever pitch—and shows no signs of slowing down. Overstimulated, under-rested, and on the brink of burnout, we’re desperately seeking antidotes to the ills of the digital era. But what if the answers to our modern-day woes lie in ancient Native American wisdom, not in a supposed cure-all gadget, supplement, or fitness routine?

For millennia, Indigenous communities have prioritized connection to nature, practiced reciprocity with community, and upheld sacred cultural traditions. We can all embrace these holistic principles in our daily lives, notes Lakota/Anishinaabe wellness advocate Chelsey Luger. That’s the premise behind her latest book, Native Home: The Ancestral Art of Creating Healing Spaces. In it, she offers tangible ways to incorporate these concepts into our living spaces to promote mental, physical, spiritual, and emotional balance.

In a recent development, “Everybody in North America should understand Native American home teachings because we’re all living on this land,” indicates Luger, who is an enrolled member of the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa and a descendant of the Standing Rock Sioux Tribe. “There’s a movement in the home industry right now centered around ensuring our surroundings support our well-being. This might be an emerging conversation in the wellness space, but Indigenous communities have been living this way for centuries.”.

Luger and her husband, Onk Akimel O’odham fitness educator Thosh Collins, co-founded the grassroots initiative Well For Culture back in 2013, with the aim of revitalizing Indigenous wellness practices. Since then, they’ve been traveling to tribal nations across the country to both teach and learn from these communities. Native Home is the culmination of those lessons.

She underscores that these principles are applicable to everyone, no matter their heritage, with this caveat: The difference between appreciation and appropriation is all in the approach. “I’m not encouraging you to do exactly what Indigenous communities do,” she claims. “I’m encouraging you to apply these teachings to your own home in a way that reflects your own culture.”.

For example, in a Native worldview, every home should tell a story through its design and decor, Luger explains. Her ancestors painted their tepees with images representing their familial experiences. Similarly, the artwork adorning our walls should feel curated and specific to our identity.

With this in mind, Luger encourages people to stay intimately involved in their home’s design and decorating process, as she’s doing with her family’s in-the-works house on Arizona’s Salt River Reservation (where Collins is from). But you needn’t be building a latest abode to reap the benefits of Indigenous wellness. There are easy, everyday ways to embrace these principles—and they don’t cost a thing.

Starting small is as simple as decluttering one room to reduce sensory overload, letting in more natural sunlight to balance circadian rhythms, opening up your windows for cross-drafting airflow, or carving out an area for movement—even if it’s only a designated stretching space. Next-level applications encompass philosophies like Indigenous minimalism and Native geomancy (auspicious arrangement, akin to feng shui), which are all explained in the book.

Like most Indigenous wisdom, Luger’s advice is pretty intuitive—and yet, it isn’t how we lead our lives today. “We might say that we don’t want to overconsume, but Americans tend to think the bigger the house, the better,” she says. “Our generation is facing a housing crisis, and we should all embrace smaller living. Not only is it easier to maintain, but it keeps us better connected. That’s what this is ultimately about: interconnection.”.

Here, Luger offers five tips for incorporating Indigenous wellness in your home.

“We’ve always had a respect for the elements—air, fire, water, and earth. Air in particular is considered sacred by most Indigenous communities. Here in the United States, we use air conditioning more than most other countries in the world. It’s a wonderful luxury, but our indoor environments should better reflect the outdoors. Try keeping your windows open for part of the day, no matter the season.”.

In a recent development, “Doorways are considered portals, which are places of high energy. Growing up, my dad would hang a hand drum or a medicine wheel above our door. It’s a way to bring good energy both for those arriving and for those leaving. Honor the doorway by hanging something that represents the presence of your ancestors and offers both protection and peace.”.

It has been revealed that “It’s a very European idea to have a separate room for everything. In contrast, Indigenous homes historically tended to be more fluid, with communal rooms that foster togetherness. That interconnection is part of our values as Indigenous people. Let at least one space in your home feel more multi-use, where family members can share space.”.

“Many traditional Native structures are round, which represents women, Mother Earth, and our egalitarian values. Indigenous architect Douglas Cardinal (Métis/Blackfoot), who designed the National Museum of the American Indian in Washington, D.C., often expresses this with curvilinear forms. But you don’t have to build a round house or room. Choose a circular dining table, rugs, and pillows rather than square or rectangular ones.”.

Recent findings suggest that “As Native people, we’ve never lost that closeness to our ancestors, even through colonization and the boarding school era. That spiritual and practical connection to who we are as people is just part of our culture. Whoever you are, wherever you come from—everybody has ancestors they can and should feel connected to. Take time to learn about your culture, and then make your home a reflection of that.”.
