💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the Vogue Business Beauty Tracker, produced in collaboration with Spate, tracks the top five brands, trends and ingredients that are driving the most significant positive change in year-on-year growth that have also demonstrated consistent upward growth historically.
  • It has been revealed that it’s all about the multi-purpose fragrance this week as search data highlights growing interest in fragrances that combine practical formats, occasion-led scents, and distinctive notes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Vogue Business Beauty Tracker, produced in collaboration with Spate, tracks the top five brands, trends and ingredients that are driving the most significant positive change in year-on-year growth that have also demonstrated consistent upward growth historically. Each week, we’ll spotlight a different beauty category and the top five beauty hashtags on TikTok.

It has been revealed that it’s all about the multi-purpose fragrance this week as search data highlights growing interest in fragrances that combine practical formats, occasion-led scents, and distinctive notes. Searches for Chanel’s Coco Mademoiselle Fragrance Primer reflect demand for prep products that extend a scent’s wear, projection, and hold on the skin. Travel fragrance shows continued interest in travel-size versions of full-size scents. Meanwhile, wedding fragrance reflects demand for a dedicated signature scent for the substantial day, and white floral perfume highlights interest in scents built around blossoms such as jasmine, gardenia, and tuberose, while pineapple fragrance signals demand for bright, tropical fruit notes.

It has been revealed that for fragrance brands, there is growing interest in concept-driven scents, heritage expertise, and affordable fragrance lines. Lore fragrances inspire specific memories, moods, and places, while Toskovat, an independent niche perfume house from Romania, stands out for composing each scent as a “bottled memory”, or extrait de mémoire. Shiseido reflects interest in the Japanese house’s heritage fragrances, with searches focused on Zen. Ranger Station, based in Nashville, draws on music culture and American landscapes for its unisex, artisan-style scents. Finally, Old Navy points to demand for affordable fragrance through Old Navy Beauty Co., its line of hair and body mists, lotions, and body washes, which expanded in August 2026.

It’s all about hair and nail maintenance on TikTok this week.

Industry observers note that #KTipHairExtension reflects interest in semi-permanent extensions, with stylists showing how individual strands are bonded to natural hair using keratin tips. #CurlyHairGel and #CurlyHairVolume highlight interest in curly hair styling, from gels that keep curls defined, hydrated, and frizz-free to techniques that build lift and fullness at the root. #HolidayEyeMakeup points to interest in festive, party-ready eye looks, with tutorials circulating ahead of the winter holidays. Meanwhile, #CuticleRemover centers on at-home nail care, with videos demonstrating how to use Sally Hansen’s Instant Cuticle Remover.

In a recent development, at-home application and retro, graphic designs are among this month’s biggest nail trends. Searches for solid gel polish are on the rise, reflecting demand for a thicker, pot-based gel formula designed for more controlled application, while press-on sets remain popular for their reusability. White chrome powder, which creates a pearly, mirror-like finish when buffed over gel polish, is trending in time for the winter months, as well as geometric nail designs for their clean lines and shapes. Meanwhile, vintage nail polishes, including Urban Decay’s discontinued metallic foil shades, reinforce consumer interest in discontinued products that allow for a nostalgic aesthetic.

Recent findings suggest that for nail brands, DIY manicure solutions, art-driven designs, and everyday nail tools are proving a success. The rise of Cyprus-based brand Doonails reflects demand for do-it-yourself manicure and pedicure products designed to deliver salon-quality results. Never Have I Ever reflects demand for reusable press-on nails featuring licensed artwork from independent artists and cultural icons, while Double Rhythm underscores interest in accessible soak-off gel polishes and nail art supplies. Heyhae offers sun-cured gel nail strips that harden naturally in sunlight without requiring a traditional UV or LED lamp, and Diamond Cosmetics signals continued interest in accessible nail products that offer variety and affordability.

In a recent development, hair how-to content is ever-growing on TikTok, with creators twisting small sections of coily hair into a #coiltwist or #CurlsWithStraightener tutorials doing the rounds. Meanwhile, the rise in videos showing off #DarkBalayage points to demand for soft, dimensional color finishes on brunette and black hair, which offers a subtle look that minimizes root visibility. There’s also rising demand for lip stains that provide #AllDayLipColor, while #TestingMakeup content reveals creators trying out new viral products in their full-face routines, sharing verdicts as they go.

It has been revealed that the makeup products consumers are searching for the most are those combining precise application, long wear, and shimmering finishes. Tools such as winged eyeliner stamps take the stress and guesswork out of creating a sharp, even cat-eye look, while creamy lip liners offer buildable definition through soft, blendable formulas. Gripping primers and longwear lipsticks also reflect demand for staying power, from tacky primers that give makeup a sticky base to lip formulas designed to resist fading and transfer. Meanwhile, the rise of rose gold eyeshadow highlights interest in pink-toned metallic shades that add dimension to eye looks.

Sources indicate that when it comes to makeup brands, lasting interest in Burberry Beauty signals the strength of luxury cosmetics from established fashion houses, especially foundations. Nude by Nature highlights demand for makeup powered by natural Australian botanicals. Beauty Creations, a Latina-founded brand, stands out for high-pigment formulas, frequent limited-edition collections, and pop culture partnerships. Sculpted by Aimee, founded by makeup artist Aimee Connolly, reflects interest in multitasking, skin-first products that simplify daily routines. Finally, KeyYou points to demand for lash extension kits and cluster lashes designed for self-application.

Industry observers note that there’s a demand for the nostalgic on TikTok, with the #ThrowBackBeauty hashtag showing creators recreating and reviewing makeup, hair, and fashion looks from past decades. Over on #PerfumeTok, the fragrance community is reviewing, ranking, and recommending scents, while #BlackFridayBeautyDeals points to anticipation ahead of TikTok Shop’s official Black Friday campaign. Meanwhile, #FalseLashesTutorial reflects demand for step-by-step guidance on applying false lashes, and #ServerHairInspo highlights low-maintenance hairstyles built to last throughout the work shift — fueled by the viral “server hair theory” that certain styles can earn servers higher tips.

Skincare products that combine regenerative ingredients, targeted application, and everyday hydration are on the rise in search. Fresh PDRN formats — creams, face masks, and eye patches — reinforce interest in the ingredient, which is associated with cellular repair and a stronger skin barrier, as well as its use in targeted treatments like the Abib PDRN Retinal Eye Patch. Increased searches for hyaluronic acid face lotion reflects demand for deep hydration in everyday skincare, while liquid pimple patches highlight interest in subtle formulas that directly target blemishes and dry into an invisible film.

Sources indicate that skincare consumers are particularly intrigued in brands combining clinical-grade formulas, advanced delivery technologies, and everyday sun protection. Magic Molecule reflects continued demand for hypochlorous acid, offering a multi-purpose, FDA-cleared spray for everyday skincare. KRX Aesthetics and Meditherapy, both South Korean brands, are known for their professional skin treatments adapted for at-home use. Radical Skincare stands out for its performance-driven anti-aging formulas, powered by its proprietary Trylacel delivery technology. Finally, Invisible Zinc reflects demand for mineral-based sunscreens that use zinc oxide as the primary ingredient instead of chemical UV filters.

Over on TikTok, #DolphinSkin reflects interest in ultra-glossy, smooth, and luminous skin, specifically on the body. #GreenChromeNails and #ColorLashes highlight bold approaches to color, from mirror-like metallic manicures in shades of green to multi-colored lash looks. Content featuring #TTSKbeauty, or TikTok Shop K-beauty, highlights the platform’s growing role in K-beauty product discovery. Meanwhile, the rise of #JasmineFragrance is driven by Chun Breeze Xian Jasmine, a Chinese fragrance that creators compare to the jasmine tea scent of tea house chains Molly Tea and Heytea.

In a recent development, in haircare, products that combine scalp support, deep nourishment, and targeted cleansing are trending in search. Peptide hair serums cater to those seeking lightweight formulas that support fuller-looking hair, with searches associated primarily with The Ordinary’s Multi-Peptide Serum for Hair Density, while hair thinning serums points to a broader focus on density and scalpcare. Rice water hair spray highlights interest in a convenient leave-in format for an ingredient valued for adding strength and shine. Cholesterol hair treatment reflects demand for rich, deep-conditioning masks that restore moisture and softness, and chlorine removal shampoo signals demand for clarifying formulas that remove chlorine build-up post-swim.

When it comes to brands, the rise of K-beauty player Lilyeve reflects demand for daily scalpcare, with searches led by its Scalp Turn Cica PDRN Brush Ampoule, a cooling leave-in treatment applied through a built-in brush head. Demand for Honeyque products highlights interest in salon-grade Japanese haircare designed to repair dry, damaged and frizzy hair, while Chāmpo stands out for blending ayurvedic principles with modern trichology, particularly through its hair serum. Bare Anatomy underscores continued demand for science-backed, dermatologically tested haircare, from anti-dandruff shampoo to a roll-on scalp serum. Finally, Brickell Men’s Products reflects interest in natural grooming formulated specifically for men.

It has been revealed that beyond traditional beauty content, #MakeupGame on TikTok reflects the growing overlap between beauty and gaming, with posts centered around Makeup Mania, a Roblox game where players compete through makeup and fashion looks. #HowToSilkPress and #4CWashDay highlight continued demand for textured hair education, from step-by-step silk press tutorials to wash day routines tailored to tightly coiled 4C hair. The #GlitterAcrylic hashtag points to interest in sparkling, statement acrylic nail sets, while #EczemaPatch reveals the hydrocolloid format popularized by pimple patches expanding to eczema-prone skin.

Industry observers note that in the wellness world, there’s growing interest in specialized nutrition and brands that prioritize convenience and targeted health benefits. Pure Genius Protein reflects demand for portable, high-protein formats, with ready-to-drink shots providing 23 grams of protein per serving. Sisel highlights a broad approach to wellness through dietary supplements and functional beverages, while Toplux Nutrition emphasizes science-backed supplements at affordable prices. Wip stands out for its nicotine-free caffeine pouches, offering a convenient format for an energy boost. Finally, Triquetra Health reflects interest in gut and metabolic wellness, with searches focused on its GLP-Pro probiotic and postbiotic supplement. Collectively, these brands span everyday protein intake, energy support, and targeted nutritional supplementation.

Sources indicate that in the midst of October, #HalloweenHairClips are trending on TikTok, reflecting interest in festive, spooky hair accessories — particularly horror-themed claw clips and seasonal designs. Meanwhile, the rise of #LadybugMakeup highlights whimsical, insect-inspired makeup looks also tailored to spooky season. Across manicure content, #UglyNails are performing well, as more unconventional and unusual nail designs gain traction for allowing artistic expression, while #PinkCateyeNails reflects interest in light-reflecting cateye designs in shades of pink. The #CoilyCurly hashtag celebrates natural hair textures between curly and coily, with content focused on haircare tips and styling.

Industry observers note that products that combine hydration, targeted care and sensory experiences are ruling the bodycare category. Hydrating body mists meet demand for lightweight, water-like moisturizers that deliver lotion-level hydration, while anti-sweat hand creams offer targeted solutions for managing perspiration on the hands. Growing demand for hand mists suggest interest in convenient, fragrant formats that refresh and sanitize on the go, while niacinamide body wash is an example of products designed to support the skin’s moisture barrier. Finally, strawberry body scrub reflects demand for fruit-inspired bodycare that combines exfoliation with appealing scents and ingredients.

Industry observers note that across bodycare brands, there’s growing interest in those offering specialized and efficient approaches to personal care and grooming. Carpe reflects demand for clinical-strength sweat and odor control, while Hanni highlights simplified bodycare through “skip-step” essentials, with a particular rise in searches for its Splash Salve in-shower body balm. Proraso stands out for its Italian men’s grooming heritage. Estée Lauder has evolved its fragrance range by incorporating bodycare into its iconic scent collections, as searches for its Beautiful Perfumed Body Powder grow. Meanwhile, Prequel reflects interest in dermatologist-developed, science-backed skincare centered on skin barrier health.

This week on TikTok, the #DiscountMakeup hashtag is flooded with shoppers unexpectedly discovering Jeffree Star Cosmetics products at Dollar Tree. Meanwhile, content around #PerfumeMists is focused on reviews and recommendations of lightweight, refreshing fragrance formats. #TattooLipLiner content is also on the rise, featuring ink-like liners, peel-off stains, and semi-permanent lip treatments for long-lasting lip definition. #GlowyMakeupRoutine points to interest in luminous, radiant makeup looks and routines, while #FeatheredHair highlights interest in the ’70s voluminous, heavily layered hair look. Together, these trends highlight how beauty content is increasingly shaped by product discovery, makeup routines and nostalgic aesthetics.

There’s growing interest in fragrance trends that combine personalization, identity, and convenience. Alcohol-free fragrances, for example, reflect demand for alternative formulations to traditional perfumes, while custom perfumes point to interest in personalized scents tailored to individual preferences. The rise of masculine fragrances suggests that scent is increasingly functioning as an identity marker for male and female consumers alike, while gothic perfume reflects demand for darker and more mysterious aromatic profiles that evoke the romantic and atmospheric elements of the goth aesthetic. Finally, travel fragrances, the portable and convenient scent formats designed to make fragrance easier to pack and use on the go, are also trending.

This month, there’s particular interest in fragrance brands offering distinctive approaches to scent. Lore’s emotive, transportive fragrances translate specific moods and places into immersive scent experiences, while MCM Fragrance and Miu Miu highlight growing interest in luxury scents that extend recognizable fashion identities into fragrance, with searches for the latter mainly associated with Miutine and its youthful fragrance identity. Ranger Station stands out for its bold, high-concentration, nature-inspired scents, while Maison d’Etto offers perfumes rooted in equestrian influence, contemporary art and architecture. These brands highlight growing consumer interest in fragrance that goes beyond scent itself, offering distinctive stories, identities and sensory experiences.

Recent findings suggest that as we enter October season, #SpookyNailArt is trending on TikTok, reflecting interest in Halloween-inspired nail designs based on playful motifs. Meanwhile, growing interest in the #MakeupColorTheory reinforces the rise of consumers learning about the hues that enhance their features. #ConcertHair highlights demand for hairstyles that are durable, creative and highly accessorized, specifically designed to last throughout a concert, while the #RomanticUpdo reflects interest in soft, feminine hairstyles and intentionally undone styles. #CologneHaul highlights interest in discovering and showcasing fragrance purchases and collections.

Industry observers note that when it comes to nails, there’s a growing interest in trends that combine precision, personalization, and visually distinct finishes. The Italian manicure, which creates the appearance of longer slender nails, reflects demand for more precise techniques, while nail art pens and letters on nails point to interest in customized designs and intricate details. The rise of glass nail polish highlights a preference for glossy, translucent finishes, and vibrant nails reflect demand for bold, eye-catching colors.

Recent findings suggest that among this month’s trending nail brands, there’s a clear preference for distinct approaches to at-home manicures. Reusable, press-on nail line Never Have I Ever incorporates licensed artwork from independent artists and cultural icons into nail designs, while Double Rhythm reinforces interest in accessible, soak-off gel polishes and nail art supplies for DIY and salon-style looks. IPolish stands out for its digital color-changing press-on nails, allowing customers to switch between hundreds of shades using a smartphone and activation wand. Heyhae offers sun-cured gel nail strips that harden naturally in sunlight without requiring a traditional UV or LED lamp, while Sparkle & Co. specializes in DIY dip powders with unique glitters, foils, flakes, glow-in-the-dark, and color-changing effects.

TikTok is seeing an influx of content featuring #BumperBangs, reflecting interest in vintage 1940s and ’50s fringe styles consisting of a bold, rounded shape. Meanwhile, the rise of #CurlyHairBride highlights demand for bridal hair inspiration that embraces natural curls and textured styles. #WigsOnTikTok demonstrates the growing role of TikTok in discovering, styling, and showcasing wigs. #UltaFragrance and #SephoraBeautyAdvisor highlight interest in beauty advisors sharing recommendations, product expertise and customer interactions at retailers Ulta and Sephora. Together, these hashtags highlight interest in vintage looks, occasion-specific styling, and behind-the-scenes beauty retail experiences.

There’s a growing interest in makeup products that combine ease of use, enhanced appearance, and convenient beauty benefits, according to monthly search data. Growth in creamy lip liners points to demand for smooth, easy-to-apply products that shape and define the lips, while lip volumizers help create the appearance of fuller, smoother lips without invasive treatments. Rose gold eyeshadow is also trending, driven by demand for warm, luminous shades. Gripping primer, which is a gel-based product with a tacky finish to hold your makeup in place, reflects interest in creating durable makeup looks that last throughout the day. The rise of SPF face powder reveals interest in facial sun protection beyond conventional sunscreens, with multifunctional products that both protect and control shine.

Across makeup brands, those offering distinctive products spanning various price points are performing particularly well. Hung Vanngo Beauty reflects demand for makeup artist expertise, while Burberry Beauty signals continued interest in luxury cosmetics from established fashion houses. C-beauty brand Cheeryep and Sleek Makeup highlight demand for vibrant, high-pigment makeup and innovative finishes. Maven Beauty, Fashion Nova’s makeup brand, suggests growing demand for affordable beauty options.

On TikTok, #UVHairExtensions are gaining traction, reflecting interest in innovative UV and LED hair extension techniques offering fast application, while #BrownRedHair highlights demand for rich, warm hair color combinations of brown, red, copper, and mahogany tones. Manicurist content featuring #PracticeNails highlights past designs and their training progress, while #CottagecoreNails spotlights whimsical, nature-inspired manicures influenced by cottagecore aesthetics. The rise of #BridesmaidsMakeup reflects growing demand for beauty inspiration tailored to bridesmaids and wedding looks.

Industry observers note that in skincare, monthly interest in products and treatments that combine targeted skin health benefits with gentle, barrier-supporting ingredients and advanced technologies is rising. Silicone-free sunscreen and its lightweight, ingredient-conscious sun protection is trending, while the retinol sandwich method, where retinol is layered between moisturizer to reduce the risk of irritation, is gaining traction among those looking to safely introduce retinol into their routines. There is continued demand for hyaluronic acid face lotions offering convenient, hydrating properties that support moisture retention and skin plumpness, while ceramide toners are designed to strengthen and maintain the skin barrier. Interest in high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) treatments highlights demand for advanced, non-invasive aesthetic treatments focused on skin tightening and rejuvenation.

Industry observers note that for brands, those offering science-backed and targeted skincare solutions are trending. Elm Biosciences, which develops clinical skincare focused on healthy aging and cellular-level care, is gaining traction, while Magic Molecule offers hypochlorous acid solutions that cleanse, reduce inflammation and support skin healing. The rise of TropicSport signals demand for high-performance sun protection during active lifestyles. NewGel+ reflects interest in specialized scarcare and skin repair. The Body Shop, particularly its Drops of Youth line, highlights demand for products targeting early signs of aging while supporting skin resilience against daily environmental stressors.

Sources indicate that on TikTok, #SheinMakeupHaul is trending, reflective of the growing interest in discovering and sharing affordable makeup products through beauty hauls. #BestHairOils shows how more consumers are comparing different hair oils and seeking product recommendations. #BakedBlush features content spotlighting latest blush launches and shades comparisons through product swatches and reviews. #TinselBraids and #CakeNails highlight playful approaches to self-expression through decorative hairstyles and creative nail designs, with consumers exploring visually distinctive looks.

Industry observers note that this month’s search data highlights growing interest in haircare products that combine targeted follicle growth with plant-based ingredients. Popular hair serums range from including specific active ingredients, with searches for redensyl and peptide serums that help reduce shedding by supporting follicle health and improving fullness, to concern-specific searches such as hair thinning serum. Rice water hairspray highlights demand for convenient, multifunctional products that can strengthen strands, add shine and reduce frizz, while plant-based shampoos reflect growing interest in products made primarily with vegan and botanical ingredients.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to haircare brands, those offering performance-driven, science-backed and premium solutions, in particular, are trending. Labo-H reflects demand for Korean scalpcare and hair loss prevention, while UltraSwim highlights interest in cleansing products designed to remove chlorine, chemical odors, and mineral buildup from hair. Bare Anatomy signals demand for science-backed haircare, addressing specific concerns such as shedding, dandruff, frizz, and damage, while Bvlgari Beauty reflects interest in luxury products combining cleansing and scalpcare with the brand’s signature scents. Meanwhile, Iso Beauty highlights growing interest in solutions that deliver salon-quality results at home.

It has been revealed that over on TikTok, #BabyShowerMakeup reflects interest in soft glam makeup looks tailored specifically for mothers and guests attending baby showers, while #MarchMakeup shows makeup looks based on the birthday month. #QuickCurls highlights demand for fast and easy hairstyling techniques for curly hair, while #LakeHair reflects interest in solutions to avoid or untangle the messy, textured, and sometimes dry or mineral-coated hair associated with freshwater swimming. #AntioxidantSerum shows dermatologist content discussing skincare products centered around antioxidant benefits and protection from environmental stressors.

Sources indicate that across wellness, monthly search data highlights growing interest in products that combine targeted benefits, convenience, and ease of use. Dopamine patches, for example, reflect demand for wearable solutions associated with mood and focus support, while acupressure wristbands reveal interest in convenient solutions for managing and preventing nausea, particularly concerning travel and motion sickness. Screenless fitness trackers demonstrate growing demand for minimalist wearable technology that passively monitors health and activity data without the distraction of a screen. Men’s fertility supplements signal interest in targeted nutritional support for male reproductive health, while liquid zinc supplements highlight demand for convenient ways to prevent or address zinc deficiency and support immune health.

According to recent reports, for brands, there’s growing interest in those offering targeted, convenient, and science-backed wellness solutions. Pure Genius Protein reflects demand for portable, easy-to-consume protein products, while Artemis Tea highlights interest in organic herbal teas and wellness blends rooted in traditional herbalism. According to recent reports, over on TikTok, the growing traction for #BridalUpdoStyle reflects interest in polished, occasion-ready hairstyles for weddings and special events. #FauxBrows and #HowToSelfTan highlight different approaches to enhancing everyday beauty, from creating realistic, hair-like brow strokes to achieving an even, natural-looking tan at home. #MakeupPR reflects the influencer culture around receiving and unboxing gifted beauty products, as well as creators sharing their experiences with brands. #MakeupOver35 highlights growing interest in makeup techniques and product recommendations tailored to women over the age of 35.

Industry observers note that in the bodycare space, current search trends highlight growing interest in products that combine targeted benefits and convenience with sensory appeal. Alpha hydroxy (AHA) body lotions and hand exfoliators reflect demand for exfoliating and smoothing products that help remove dead skin cells, dirt, and dry patches. Grape soap highlights playful, fruit-inspired formats that combine functionality with novelty and aesthetics. According to recent reports, as for bodycare brands, those offering targeted, skin-friendly solutions are gaining traction. These brands reveal how the category is evolving through specialist treatments based on body area and skin concern, spanning natural-based products to dermatologist-designed solutions.

Over on TikTok, #VampNails reflect interest in bold, dramatic nail looks inspired by dark and vampy aesthetics. #RootRetouch and #GrayGrowOut highlight different approaches to managing hair color, from concealing visible roots to embracing the transition to natural gray. #HairVolumeHacks signals demand for accessible styling techniques that create fuller, more voluminous hair. #MakeupTrial reflects interest in testing and refining makeup looks ahead of weddings and special events.

This month’s search data highlights a shift toward more occasion-driven and emotionally evocative fragrance choices. The rise of wedding fragrances reflects growing interest in scents associated with meaningful celebrations and special occasions. Electric perfume, meanwhile, with searches mainly associated with the iconic Revlon fragrance from the 80s, Electric Youth, reflects the enduring appeal of discontinued scents that offer a upcoming form of nostalgia.

In a recent development, on TikTok, #CreamEyeshadowSticks are trending, as demand rises for convenient, easy-to-apply makeup formats that allow consumers to create smooth, buildable eye looks with minimal effort. #ChunkyHighlights and #NailFoils reflect growing interest in creative beauty techniques that add dimension and visual impact to hair and nails. #UltaHairSalon reflects consumers’ and salon workers’ experiences with hair services in retail stores, highlighting a convenient way to access professional salon expertise. Meanwhile, celestial nails signal increasing enthusiasm for imaginative and artistic nail designs inspired by cosmic themes and metallic accents.

Gluten-free lipstick highlights rising awareness of ingredient sensitivities, while medium-coverage concealer points to a preference for balanced, skin-like finishes. Meanwhile, the rise of cool-toned blush underscores a want for precise shade matching, as consumers seek out colors that better complement their undertones. Together, these trends indicate that makeup is evolving toward customized, results-driven routines that combine performance, personalization, and ingredient-conscious choices.

Industry observers note that the rise of Tilt Beauty reflects a shift toward accessible, inclusive design, showing that consumers value products tailored to different abilities and needs. Skindinavia demonstrates a preference for long-lasting, professional-grade finishes. Caia Cosmetics highlights a demand for accessible, high-quality makeup that delivers an effortless, glowing look similar to Jung Saem Mool, which leans into a Korean expertise that delivers natural, glowing skin. Rodan + Fields signals an interest in hybrid complexion products combining coverage with skincare benefits. Overall, makeup is evolving toward accessible, glow-focused, and treatment-infused routines that blend professional performance with everyday wearability.

It has been revealed that on TikTok, the rise of #LocDetoxing reflects a demand for deep-cleansing routines that support scalp and hair health, particularly among protective styles. #HairPlop highlights an interest in techniques that enhance natural texture, especially for defining curls with minimal effort. #TakingDownBraids points to maintenance-focused content, as consumers navigate the full lifecycle of protective styles. #SunscreenApplication underscores growing attention to proper usage and technique in daily skincare routines, while #AirbrushSprayTan focuses on in-process guidance, from what to wear to how to ensure even results. Together, these hashtags show that consumers are seeking guidance across application and maintenance in beauty content.

In a recent development, in skincare, current search data reveals a rising focus on advanced, treatment-led products. Interest in scar sticks reflects demand for targeted solutions that simplify care for specific concerns. PDRN cream and serum signal growing awareness of regenerative ingredients, as consumers seek formulas tied to skin repair and renewal. Exosome serum highlights increasing interest in next-generation, science-backed actives, while high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) underscores the influence of non-invasive, clinic-inspired technologies, as consumers look for lifting and firming benefits beyond topical products. Together, these trends indicate that skincare is evolving toward highly targeted, science-driven routines that blend efficacy, innovation, and treatment-level results.

According to recent reports, ELM Biosciences underscores the growing interest in science-backed, clinically developed skincare, with a “lab-to-patient” approach supporting long-term skin health and the concept of aging well. AO Skincare signals demand for antioxidant-rich formulas that strengthen skin resilience against environmental stressors. Organic Apoteke reflects continued interest in holistic, ayurvedic-inspired skincare, as consumers seek gentle solutions for concerns like acne and sensitivity. Yepoda Skincare and Tosowoong, both Korean brands, highlight the influence of active-led formulations and high-concentration products targeting concerns such as acne, pigmentation, and aging.

Industry observers note that on TikTok, #MicroLinksHairExtensions are trending, reflecting demand for natural-looking length and volume, as consumers invest in seamless hair enhancements. #ViralDollarTreeMakeup highlights budget-conscious beauty discovery, with people testing affordable products. #HairWashDays points to routine-driven content, as consumers build and share structured care rituals for healthier hair. #PlumperLips underscores ongoing interest in enhancement-focused beauty, whether through techniques or product-driven results, while #MomHairHack spans both child hair solutions and quick, practical styling for moms themselves. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing performance, affordability, and routine-friendly approaches to beauty content.

In a recent development, current search data reveals a haircare consumer increasingly focused on targeted, treatment-led products. Interest in protein-free shampoo reflects demand for gentler formulations tailored to specific hair needs, particularly for those avoiding protein overload. Amino acid shampoo signals a shift toward ingredient-led repair, as consumers seek formulas that strengthen and support hair health. Dry shampoo paste highlights demand for multi-functional refresh solutions that absorb oil and add texture. Meanwhile, overnight hair serum shows growing interest in treatments that work during sleep, delivering hydration, repair, and frizz reduction without requiring extra time in the morning routine, and red light therapy hats underscore the rising adoption of tech-enabled solutions for scalp health and hair growth. Together, these trends indicate that haircare is evolving toward personalized, treatment-driven routines that combine efficacy, convenience, and innovation.

Playa Beauty reflects interest in California-inspired products promising effortless “beach hair”, supporting minimalist routines while enhancing natural waves and movement. California Baby underscores demand for gentle, plant-based products suitable for babies, children, and adults with sensitive skin. Ducray points to a growing appetite for clinically backed, condition-specific solutions, offering dermatologically tested treatments for dandruff, hair loss, and sensitive scalps. Dr. Groot, a Korean brand, highlights a consumer focus on scalp health and anti-hair loss solutions. Indian-inspired ayurvedic haircare brand Champo uses ingredients such as myrobalan fruit extract, gum arabic, and geranium oil to resonate with a consumer seeking easy packaged haircare, rather than performing weekly ayurvedic hair oiling. California Naturals signals interest in natural, nourishing formulas that strengthen hair.

Sources indicate that on TikTok, #DitchedTheDye reflects a shift among older women embracing their natural hair color and moving away from maintenance-heavy routines. #ILoveCurlyHair highlights a growing appreciation for natural texture, as consumers celebrate and care for their curls. #PromMakeupInspo points to planning and inspiration for key events, with users seeking polished, occasion-ready looks. #CubanTwistHair underscores interest in protective styling and cultural hair practices, while #HairFoam signals demand for styling products that enhance texture and hold. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing self-expression, hair health, and event-driven styling in beauty content.

Consumers are increasingly seeking convenient, easy-to-use formats and wearable solutions for functional wellness, with patches offering targeted support for mood, metabolism and cellular health. Dopamine patches target focus and cognitive performance, while GLP-1 and NAD patches support metabolism, energy and cellular function. Cutting Jelly reflects interest in supplements for weight management and fat reduction and pressotherapy points to growing demand for non-invasive recovery and circulation-boosting treatments. These trends show wellness routines evolving beyond basic supplementation toward a focus on energy to fat reduction and enhanced circulation.

Javvy Coffee reflects growing interest in functional beverages that combine everyday rituals with wellness benefits, offering convenient ways to support energy and focus. A1 Supplements and MTS Nutrition underscore demand for performance-driven sports nutrition, including muscle building, bodybuilding and post-workout recovery, appealing to consumers seeking results-oriented solutions. Lullabites points to a desire for wellness products that support rest and recovery, emphasizing functional snacks designed for relaxation and sleep. IM8 Health, co-founded by David Beckham, highlights interest in simplified, all-in-one nutrition that combines multiple supplements into a single, convenient daily drink. What’s That Patch is delivering patches packed with nutrients that help with sleep, stress, productivity and more. Together, these brands reveal that wellness consumers are seeking products that are functional, evidence-based and seamlessly integrated into daily routines.

#LashGlues highlights interest in product performance and comparison between brands, as consumers test glues for reliable, long-lasting lash applications. #MakeupSamples reflects budget-conscious discovery, with shoppers exploring trial sizes and low-commitment ways to test products. #HairTrial points to planning and preparation, as consumers test styles ahead of key moments. Meanwhile, #HerbalHairGrowthOil signals demand for natural, treatment-focused solutions, and #BushyBrows spans interest from managing and shaping fuller brows to enhancing volume and testing products. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing performance, planning and creativity in beauty content.

There’s an increasing focus on functional, treatment-led bodycare products that deliver targeted results. Interest in epsom salt lotions reflects a demand for convenient, topical solutions that soothe sore muscles and support recovery. Searches for kojic acid lotions and turmeric body washes signal a growing focus on brightening and tone correction across the body, as consumers turn to ingredient-led solutions that address hyperpigmentation and uneven skin tone. Silicone loofahs and glass foot files point to a preference for hygienic, durable tools that elevate cleansing and exfoliation, while addressing concerns around bacteria and skin safety.

Recent findings suggest that the rise of Crowned Skin reflects a shift toward multifunctional bodycare, as well as an interest in products like body butter colognes, which combine deep hydration with long-lasting fragrance. Bepanthol highlights demand for clinically backed, multi-purpose solutions that protect and regenerate sensitive or compromised skin. Vermont Soap underscores an interest in gentle, non-irritating cleansers and bar soaps that replace harsher detergents, reflecting a move toward safer, skin-friendly formulations. Meanwhile, Luna Daily and Kate McLeod point to growing desire for specialized and ritualized bodycare — from microbiome-balancing formulas safe for all areas of the body, to waterless, solid moisturizers that emphasize sustainability and sensorial experience.

#CheapBeauty is trending on TikTok, showing that consumers are exploring budget-conscious cosmetic options and highlighting an interest in affordable products. #SkincareComedy reflects engagement with humorous, relatable beauty moments, where audiences enjoy playful takes on everyday experiences. #HairExtensionInstallation points to professional, technique-focused content, as viewers watch skilled stylists demonstrate expert application and installation. Meanwhile, #SkinTighteningTreatment and #VolumeWispy capture aspirational results, from creams that enhance skin firmness to professional lash services that create full, wispy volume, proving that beauty audiences remain captivated by visible, high-impact transformations. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing entertainment, affordability, and aspirational transformations across beauty content.

Sources indicate that there’s a craving for gourmand fragrances taking place, as rich, edible-inspired scents capture consumer attention. Searches for masculine fragrances suggest that scent is functioning as an identity marker for male consumers, driving greater interest in variety and personalization. Tomato perfume reflects curiosity around hyper-specific, ingredient-led scents that invite consumers to reimagine familiar smells in a new context. Solid fragrances, meanwhile, point to demand for portable alternatives to spray bottles, where fragrance layering can extend beyond the home. Finally, clean, fresh perfumes reveal how consumers are seeking out fresh, lighter options as a counterpoint to rich, gourmand notes.

The popularity of Middle Eastern houses like Arabiyat Prestige, Gulf Orchid, and Assaf highlights a consumer shift toward heritage-rich fragrances known for their high-concentration and long-lasting power. YCZ captures the rise of social media-driven accessibility, proving that viral scents can provide high-quality alternatives to designer perfumes at an affordable price point. Narcotica underscores the appeal of the niche Italian market, where the focus is on “addictive”, high-concentration gourmands that blend bold sweetness with luxurious, long-lasting ingredients.

#TrippyNails are trending, showing that consumers are drawn to surreal, psychedelic nail aesthetics that use distorted patterns and holographic finishes to create eye-catching results. #EasterMakeup reflects a fascination with seasonal, pastel-driven makeup, highlighting how soft color palettes and whimsical details capture attention during spring celebrations. #MakeupCleansingBalm points to growing interest in high-performance cleansers that remove heavy makeup without drying out the skin or leaving it feeling stripped. Meanwhile, #GRWMDate and #HairGoneWrong capture unfiltered, relatable beauty experiences. The former centers on personal storytelling and dating life while getting ready, and the latter highlights the reality of styling mishaps, illustrating how beauty audiences value both the social side of getting ready and the more candid moments that happen along the way.

It has been revealed that what’s drawing consumers in? According to data, its playful and creative nail expressions. There’s increased interest in stained glass and matcha nails, as people seek visually striking, color-rich designs that combine artistry with trend-driven aesthetics. Meanwhile, polka dot nails highlight a preference for playful patterns that add personality to everyday manicures. The rise of nail art pens signals a move toward precision and customization. Finally, solid gel nail glue indicates attention to durable, reliable application, showing that consumers value long-lasting performance alongside unique nail looks.

In terms of brands, the rise of Heyhae reflects a shift toward convenient, at-home nail solutions, as more consumers value semi-cured gel strips, which can be applied under natural sunlight for quick, non-toxic manicures. Diamond Cosmetics highlights the demand for affordable, everyday nail tools, making professional-grade manicures accessible to a wide audience. Nail Reformation demonstrates interest in high-quality, reusable press-on nails, offering a salon-level, damage-free experience at home. Meanwhile, Sunuv and IBD Beauty underscore the appeal of salon-level equipment and innovations — from UV and LED lamps to builder gel.

It has been revealed that this week on TikTok, #RobeCurls are trending, as more consumers are drawn to heatless styling techniques that simplify hair routines while delivering defined, natural-looking results. #IceCreamNails reflects a fascination with playful, dessert-inspired nail aesthetics, which underscore how novelty textures and creative color palettes capture attention across nail content. The #LipOilGloss hashtag spotlights lip products that combine shine, nourishment, and a lightweight feel in everyday routines. Meanwhile, #SoftBridalMakeup and #GenZMakeup captures two parallel beauty directions: one centered on polished, natural elegance for milestone events, and the other revealing side-by-side contrasts between Gen Z and millennial makeup styles. Together, these trends show how consumers are balancing practical beauty solutions, playful visual trends, and cross-generational style influences.

Subtle, natural-looking makeup continues to be popularized by medium-coverage products such as concealers. The rise of cool-toned blush and illuminating drops further signals a move toward color theory-informed customization, where consumers use specific undertones and light-reflecting finishes to create a healthy and natural glow. There’s also demand for clean mascara, where lightweight, ingredient-conscious formulas are favored. Another trend on the rise is gluten-free lipsticks, pointing to growing attention to health-conscious formulations.

Industry observers note that the rise of Tilt Beauty reflects a shift toward accessible, inclusive design, showing that consumers value products tailored to different abilities and needs. Jolie Beauty highlights the demand for alternative, high-performance makeup that allows bold self-expression while remaining vegan and cruelty-free. Skindinavia demonstrates a preference for long-lasting, professional-grade finishes, while Jung Saem Mool underscores the appeal of luxury Korean expertise that delivers natural, glowing skin. Meanwhile, Concrete Minerals signals a move toward transparent formulations with bold pigments, as shoppers increasingly prioritize ingredient-conscious choices.

Industry observers note that #RushedMakeup reveals that consumers are drawn to quick, ready-to-go routines that demonstrate how to look polished fast. #NailTechASMR reflects fascination with sensory content. #BeforeAndAfterFacelift signals that audiences are intrigued by dramatic visual transformations of cosmetic procedures. #SisterLockRetightening and #WigLaid highlights a strong interest in professional hair care expertise and the maintenance of intricate, high-effort hairstyles, while also capturing attention to precision and seamless style by showcasing how flawlessly wigs are styled and finished.

The rise of scar sticks, PDRN serums, and liquid microneedling reflects a consumer increasingly invested in skin regeneration, barrier repair, and clinically backed ingredients. The portability and ease of scar sticks signal demand for convenient, targeted solutions, while liquid microneedling highlights appetite for professional-level collagen stimulation and enhanced absorption without in-clinic procedures. Growing interest in milk sunscreens signals demand for high-performance UV protection that feels lightweight, skincare-forward, and multifunctional. There’s also growth in matte lip balms, with Celine launching refillable matte lip balms accompanied by a special installation at Harrods on March 2.

Trending skincare brands reflect a shift toward clinically grounded, barrier-focused skin health paired with sustainability and device-led innovation. Genabelle and Tosowoong, both K-beauty brands, exemplify this movement: Genabelle develops science-backed, microbiome and PDRN-driven formulas designed to repair the skin barrier, while Tosowoong targets brightening, anti-aging, acne, and dehydration. At the same time, the growing attention around Shark’s CryoGlow LED mask, targeting acne, fine lines and puffiness, reflects a desire for professional-grade treatments that accelerate results, reduce inflammation, and replicate clinic-grade procedures. Meanwhile, Bolt Beauty’s biodegradable single-dose capsules and Yepoda’s K-beauty-inspired active formulations underscore the rising ingredient literacy of consumers.

In a recent development, on TikTok, the #FlawlessBraids hashtag is largely driven by hair stylists showcasing intricate braiding techniques, alongside AI-generated concepts of futuristic braiding devices that don’t yet exist — but imagine faster styling without sacrificing precision. Meanwhile, #NeonHairColor highlights bold experimentation and personal expression, while #GlowSunscreen reflects a skin-first mindset where protection and radiance are expected to work hand in hand. #ShadowLiner signals interest in detailed, technique-focused eye artistry, as creators break down application methods for more defined eye looks. #LipEssentials points to demand for streamlined, everyday lipcare that balances performance with convenience.

Recent findings suggest that the surge in beauty tools like red light therapy hats suggests that consumers are increasingly seeing the scalp as the biological foundation of hair quality, density, and longevity, embracing device-led, clinically inspired solutions they can use conveniently at home. Interest in ingredient-specific shampoo formulas featuring batana oil and amino acid, or those that are protein-free, reflects a more educated haircare buyer. Meanwhile, demand for hair smoothing serums points to a parallel desire for immediate polish and manageability. Together, these trends reveal a consumer who approaches haircare through targeted, science-backed and ingredient-conscious solutions.

It has been revealed that seapuri and Dr. Groot, both Korean brands, tap into the rising demand for scalp-focused, anti-hair loss care. Seapuri uses hydrating, mineral-rich formulas, including a water-based scalp serum to reduce hair loss and balance sebum, while Dr. Groot focuses on scalp-nourishing shampoos and targeted anti-hair loss solutions with a clinically inspired, results-driven approach. LED brands like CurrentBody, Shark, Solawave, Vym, Monastery and FAQ have also been leading the charge. Roz sits at the intersection of plant-based sustainability and professional performance delivering botanical-powered results that promote lasting scalp health. This positioning bridges the gap between the accessible, plant-based approach of California Naturals and the salon-quality focus of ISO Beauty — underscoring how consumers increasingly seek conscious formulations alongside visible, high-performance results.

On TikTok, hashtags like #BraiderOfTikTok and #BridalGlamLook are largely driven by professionals showcasing intricate techniques and polished transformations, suggesting that customers turn to the platform for inspiration. Meanwhile, #TryingNewHairstyles highlights a culture of experimentation and style switch-ups, while #SkincareMasks documents selfcare routines as part of an ongoing beauty journey. #RedHeadMascara points to growing demand for hyper-specific, shade-inclusive products, revealing that consumers are actively searching for solutions tailored to their unique features.

It has been revealed that there’s a growing interest in topical, bioactive wellness formats, with patches incorporating GLP-1s and NAD reflecting a shift to skin-applied solutions for metabolic support, longevity, and targeted physiological optimization. At the same time, consumers are searching for supplements such as oregano oil and L-theanine powder, pointing to continued demand for immune resilience and stress management through more traditional, scientifically informed formats. Cutting jelly, a Korean wellness supplement, is gaining traction for its appetite-suppressing, digestion-supporting, and fat-management proposition. Its popularity highlights a broader preference for convenient, flavorful, and results-driven wellness rituals. Collectively, these trends reflect a consumer mindset that blends experimentation with intentionality, seeking measurable benefits through both topical innovation and functional nutrition.

Sources indicate that the latest search trends show that consumers are treating wellness as a seamless part of daily life rather than a task. By brand, Javvy Coffee reflects a desire to turn everyday rituals into functional routines that boost physical performance, while Wellah signals interest in precise, results-driven nutrition for recovery and hydration. Lullabites points to a focus on restorative sleep supporting energy and clarity for the day ahead. Crisp Power highlights the rise of indulgent snacks that also meet fitness goals, and Magic Spoon shows that nostalgic, enjoyable foods are increasingly expected to deliver health benefits without compromising taste.

On TikTok, hashtags like #PinkAndPurpleHair and #PersonalizedFragrance are driven by users embracing beauty as a form of self-expression and creativity, from bold hair colors and custom scents to playful hair accessories like bows. Trends such as #LipLinerPencil highlight a desire to explore colors and combinations for defined, polished looks. Meanwhile, content around #RetentionTips indicated that beauty consumers value expert guidance and skillful maintenance, ensuring they get the most out of specialized treatments such as lash extensions.

Consumers are going beyond basic hygiene in search of specialized products, like Epsom salt lotions for muscle recovery. The rising interest in PH-balanced body washes and fungal infection lotions highlights a shift toward dermatological wellness. At the same time, tools like the glass foot file are gaining traction, reflecting a consumer focus on at-home pedicures and skin maintenance. Meanwhile, the demand for Moroccan black soap underscores a desire for ‘heritage efficacy’, where consumers seek out natural, ritual-based exfoliation to minimize synthetic chemical alternatives. These trends signal a more literate consumer who views the entire body — not just the face — as a landscape for clinical, preventative, and holistic care.

The rising search interest in brands like GoPure Beauty, QV Skincare, Diptyque, Susanne Kaufmann, and Bliss reflects a consumer shift toward the skinification of the body, whereby people demand high-performance active ingredients for use beyond their face. This behavior indicates a shift to clinical wellness, with shoppers balancing a need for dermatological efficacy and targeted solutions with a desire for the sensory luxury and ‘clean’ prestige offered by Diptyque and Susanne Kaufmann.

On TikTok, content featuring hashtags like #HairExtensionInstallation and #BrowThreading are dominated by professionals sharing techniques, as more consumers use the platform to get inspiration or find services. In contrast, #MixedHairstyles and #HairExtensionsHack are mostly driven by consumers exploring practical options and DIY approaches to at-home styling. Elsewhere, #CrueltyFreeCosmetics reflect a growing interest in ethical and sustainable products, showing that conscious choices are increasingly part of beauty conversations online.

In a recent development, the rise in sweet fragrance searches shows consumers are craving comfort and indulgence. Interest in tomato perfume and milk fragrances points to a growing appetite for unconventional, nostalgic aromas that blur the line between food and scent. The emergence of edible perfume — designed to be safely consumed — signals a shift toward playful, multisensory experiences in which application extends scent beyond the skin. Meanwhile, demand for white floral perfume suggests that classic, elegant profiles continue to anchor consumer preferences amid experimentation.

The popularity of Middle Eastern houses like Arabiyat Prestige, Gulf Orchid, and Assaf highlights a shift toward luxurious and statement-making scents. Assaf, in particular, offers luxurious, often unisex fragrances that combine oud and incense with contemporary, international notes. The rise of Xinu, meanwhile, points to a growing interest in artisanal storytelling and plant-based ingredients. Also on the rise is XO Khloé, underscoring the continued power of celebrity-led fragrance lines.

Recent findings suggest that the rise of #PinkNailDesign and #BraidsAndBows highlights playful, creative styles, while #GenZMakeup favors fresh-faced, natural looks with fun touches like graphic eyeliner, pastels, and faux freckles. The growth in #JLoMakeup is being driven by Jennifer Lopez’s Golden Globes look, which was inspired by the early-aughts supermodel glam that people are eager to recreate. The growth of #FirstTimeBotox signals increasing openness and transparency around cosmetic procedures, as users frame treatments as relatable milestones rather than taboo transformations. Meanwhile, #HoneyHairMask highlights a parallel interest in plant-based, at‑home haircare rituals focused on nourishment and maintenance.

Consumers are going for self‑expression, playful motifs and hybrid styles when it comes to nail art. Searches for cat eye heart nails, pink cat eye nails, and cat claw nails show that consumers are blending shape‑driven trends with tactile finishes, embracing looks that feel both edgy and whimsical. Meanwhile, strawberry shortcake nails point to a nostalgia‑infused trend. The interest in Cynthia Erivo nails highlights how celebrity‑inspired nail looks can drive demand, with owners translating red carpet or character‑driven aesthetics into their own manicure repertoire.

According to recent reports, the top‑growing nail brands reflect a consumer shift toward at‑home expertise and expressive finishes. Heyhae’s popularity signals a desire for playful, design-forward polishes and tutorials that help customers translate looks for everyday wear. Gaoy and Rossi Nails underscore the rise of DIY gel systems and professional‑grade kits, revealing that consumers seek salon‑quality results at home. Jodsone’s ascent points to a craving for art‑centric, niche lacquer brands that stand out with unique color stories. Meanwhile, IBD Beauty highlights continued demand for reliable, performance‑driven products in the professional and enthusiast space, especially among gels and long‑wear finishes.

On TikTok, trending beauty hashtags reveal a consumer mindset that blends identity‑driven aesthetics, routine conservation and sensory‑led selfcare. The popularity of #PastelGothMakeup shows how users are embracing expressive beauty looks, using makeup as a form of cultural and creative identity. Hashtags like #SkincareRestock and #ShampooRoutine points to the importance of consistency and ritual. #StrawberryScents highlights an interest in nostalgic fragrance profiles, while #BasketballHairstyle reflects the influence of purpose‑driven, activity‑ready beauty content.

Consumers are getting creative thanks to the popularity of peel-off lip tints and liners. The rise of blue lip stain, which applies blue but reveals a pink or berry hue once peeled, speaks to the demand for color-shifting, pH-reactive formulas that feel personalized and surprising. Plumping lip liner reflects a desire for makeup that mimics cosmetic procedures, with consumers drawn to products that visibly enhance lip volume without injections. Meanwhile, plum mascara demonstrates how consumers are exploring non-traditional but wearable color accents.

Recent findings suggest that the top-growing makeup brands reveal a consumer shift toward inclusive design, minimalist aesthetics, as well as age and tool-specific solutions. Tilt Beauty reflects rising demand for accessible, user-friendly packaging and refillable formats that are sustainable. Sweed Beauty appeals to a growing audience seeking the no-makeup makeup look, through vegan formulations that deliver barely-there finishes for natural enhancement over heavy coverage. Maange shows that consumers are investing in quality makeup brushes and application tools, signaling increased interest in the techniques behind the look, not just the formulas themselves. Meanwhile, Jung Saem Mool attracts those drawn to editorial-inspired, K-beauty artistry, and Prime Prometics caters to the needs of mature skin, emphasizing that makeup shoppers are increasingly seeking products that serve their specific life stage and texture needs.

In a recent development, the rise of #HairExtensionsTutorial and #TakingOutBraids highlights that customers are actively seeking step‑by‑step guidance for maintenance and technique. #FrenchHairPin and #PurpleHairDye underscore a growing appetite for aesthetic experimentation and trend‑inspired looks, where tools and color become playful ways to express personal style. Meanwhile, #UltaHairSalon points to the influence of in‑salon experiences and professional authority in shaping consumer choices, with users looking to bridge DIY learning and expert execution.

Industry observers note that skincare products that blend restorative care, gentle technology and everyday indulgence are on the rise. The popularity of scar sticks and PDRN serums points to the advancement in regenerative treatments that support healing and skin repair. Tools like ultrasonic skin scrubbers highlight consumers’ appetite for at‑home derm‑tech devices. Also, melting lip balms and pore care are trending as consumers seek results‑driven everyday products.

Brands with ingredients-conscious efficacy, modernized wellness and at-home performance solutions are being sought after. Terra Lotus, powered by beef tallow-based care, signals a growing interest in animal-derived, nutrient-dense skincare rooted in traditional practices, as consumers seek richer, bioavailable alternatives to plant oils and lab-created moisturizers.

According to recent reports, APLB and Genabelle continue to spike interest in science-backed K-beauty, especially products targeting hydration, brightening, and skin regeneration through actives like niacinamide and glutathione. Dermagist points to sustained interest in cosmeceutical-style anti-aging solutions. Finally, Shark Beauty’s expansion into skincare devices reflects the growing appeal of tech-enhanced and at-home treatments.

Consumers are eager to participate in viral beauty without overspending, as #AffordableLipOil and #AffordableMascara make strong cases for accessible versions of trendy, functional products. #ProfessionalHairProducts point to a growing appetite for salon-quality care. In contrast, #HydroDermabrasion reflects a rising interest for in-spa skincare treatments, as consumers turn to TikTok to understand the benefits of medical-grade exfoliation and glow-boosting facials. Meanwhile, #CranberryMakeup underscores the continued influence of seasonal and mood-based beauty aesthetics, as customers experiment with rich, warm tones to express personal style.

Exfoliating foot masks and hand masks are on a spike, as consumers approach the treatments with the same ritualistic care traditionally given to the face. Vegan body wash and magnesium body butter reflect a shift toward wellness‑aligned, ingredient‑conscious products. Meanwhile, exfoliating body lotion bridges treatment and care, showing the consumer’s need for multifunctional products that improve texture and moisture in a single step.

Kate McLeod and Brown Sugar Babe offer sensory bodycare experiences, from exfoliating stones to whipped butters. Brands like Dettol and Noshinku show that trusted hygiene and germ‑defense solutions remain top of mind. Bend Soap Company’s artisanal approach highlights the appeal of small‑batch, craft formulations.

Recent findings suggest that these top‑growing TikTok beauty hashtags reveal a consumer mindset that values efficacy, personalization, real‑world practicality and community‑driven discovery. The popularity of #ScienceBasedSkincare and #SkincareApp highlights that customers are increasingly seeking data‑informed products and digital tools. At the same time, #LazyGirlSkincare and #ThinHairTips reflect a demand for simple, low‑effort solutions that fit into busy lifestyles or specific concerns. On the makeup side, #BlushLovers highlights the enduring appeal of color cosmetics.

The surge in interest for marshmallow perfume and chocolate perfume reflects a continuous craving for gourmand, dessert‑inspired scents. The rise of rose vanilla perfume and bridal perfume suggests people are gravitating toward romantic and memory‑evoking fragrances. Growing searches for oil‑based perfume show an increased interest in long‑lasting and body‑centric scent formats, revealing a preference for fragrance that melds seamlessly with one’s natural scent and lasts longer than traditional sprays.

In a recent development, matière Première takes on the farm‑to‑fragrance purity and minimalist luxury, with its raw material‑focused compositions. La Sultane de Saba Paris channels consumer interest with olfactory-inspired notes. Similarly, The Maker Perfume hints at a growing demand for identity‑driven scent choices over mass market fragrances. Meanwhile, legacy and designer‑adjacent brands like Hugo Boss and Penhaligon’s continue to draw attention for their heritage and status, even as they explore niche alternatives.

Sensitivity-aware routines, personal customization and ingredients‑led problem-solving beauty are growing hashtags on TikTok.

According to recent reports, the popularity of #SensitiveSkincare demonstrates more people are seeking gentle, irritation‑free formulas. Meanwhile, #UnderratedSkincare suggests a hunger for hidden gems or under-the-radar products, meaning consumers are increasingly willing to explore beyond mainstream brands. The rise of #BlondeHighlightsOnDarkHair and #HairLoss captures demand for hair‑specific solutions and transformation content, as users look for guidance and community advice on challenging hair goals. Finally, #CoffeeSkincare points to the ongoing appeal of natural, functional ingredients, as people are drawn to the antioxidant and circulation‑boosting benefits of coffee in skin and hair routines.

Bold nails are back and it’s all about self‑expression and textured innovation with growing interest in statement cheetah print designs rooted in nostalgia and glamour, blending animal prints with modern finishes and clever color shifts. The appetite for animalistic styles continues with cat eye nails reflecting excitement around method‑driven finishes — using magnetic polish to create shimmering dimension that feels both futuristic and accessible. Water drop nails and junk nails are also making noise with sleek, sculptural texture for the former and a maximalist approach to the latter with oversized charms, clashing textures and extreme customization.

Sources indicate that consumers are leaning into at-home expertise and expressive finishes. Gaoy and MelodySusie highlight a growing investment in DIY tools like gel kits, lamps and drills. Nail Labo caters to a rising demand for precision and minimalist artistry, drawing from Japanese nail culture that prioritizes clean lines, quality materials and technical skill. Caudalie introduces a skincare-forward angle with its hand and nailcare rooted in antioxidant-rich formulations. Meanwhile, Ethereal Lacquer is capturing attention through its holographic, metallic and multi-chrome polishes, signaling that many nail consumers are seeking and collecting bold, light-catching finishes that double as artistic self-expression.

It has been revealed that the popularity of #OilToFoamCleanser reflects growing interest in innovative hybrid formats, suggesting consumers are drawn to easy and elevated routines. #OilySkinHack points to a problem-solving mindset, where owners seek shareable solutions tailored to specific skin concerns, especially shine and congestion. Meanwhile, #ManiInspo and #GlitterHighlighter showcase visual beauty through inspiration and self-expression, with consumers looking for aesthetic ideas that feel fresh, playful and mood-driven. Skincare-related hashtags like #Moisturiserforoilyskin, #Collagencream and #Over40skin highlight the demand for targeted, functional products that address individual skin concerns and life stages.

Recent findings suggest that among the top-growing nail trends this month, there is a desire to to strike the balance between bold self-expression and effortless sophistication. Searches for designs like cheetah print and shades such as deep red, show an interest in bold nail aesthetics that communicate personality and mood. Trends like easy gel nails, jelly gel polish and baby French nails point to a demand for low-effort, long-lasting manicures that blend simplicity with a polished, modern look.

Nailberry stands out for its focus on breathable, non-toxic formulas, emphasising the continued rise of clean beauty values even in niche categories such as nailcare.

Sources indicate that on TikTok this week, trending beauty hashtags reflect a consumer interest in visible transformation and product-driven results, seen via hashtags like #FaceliftJourney and #EyelashGrowthSerum, which emphasises before-and-after narratives through aesthetic enhancement. The popularity of #ViralDryShampoo and #MakingLipsGloss highlights enthusiasm for functional beauty hacks and DIY experimentation, where users actively seek accessible and trend-led solutions. In makeup, search trends point to a consumer preference for long-wear, low-maintenance products that deliver high performance with minimal touch-ups, as seen through the popularity of cream, black and peel-off lip stains. The growth of black and peel-off lip stains, in particular, also suggests an appetite for playful experimentation and innovative formats that merge bold aesthetics with convenience. Rising interest in creaseless concealer and blur foundation, meanwhile, reflects a desire for flawless but natural finishes, indicating a demand for skin-enhancing products that look seamless and feel lightweight.

Makeup brands like gothic-inspired Jolie Beauty and Cult Candy Cosmetics, which emphasises vegan values and niche, identity-driven beauty, reveal a desire beyond mainstream beauty aesthetics. The popularity of Wonderskin and Drmtlgy demonstrates a clear demand for innovative, long-wear and skincare-infused products, highlighting a preference for hybrid formulations that offer both cosmetic pay-off and skin benefits. The top growing beauty hashtags on TikTok reveal a consumer shift towards gentle, culturally rooted and personalised beauty practices. The rise of #IndianBeautySecrets and #WhipdBraids underscores a growing appreciation for traditional, heritage-inspired techniques and protective styles, reflecting beauty as a form of identity and cultural pride. Meanwhile, #RosaceaJourney indicates a demand for transparent, real-life narratives, where users seek connection and shared experience around sensitive skincare.

Recent findings suggest that in skincare, there is a consumer shift towards treatment-style products that delivers visible, often immediate results. Tools and products like face taping and cryo masks reflect a rising interest in non-invasive techniques that mimic professional treatments at home. Meanwhile, collagen masks and Korean face masks underscore the appeal of intensive hydration and skin renewal, often rooted in ritualistic or sensorial selfcare. Brands like AHC, Skin1004 and Aestura showcase the continued appeal of Korean skincare, valued for its soothing, barrier-supportive formulations and dermatological credibility.

Recent findings suggest that the popularity of hypochlorous acid spray signals growing awareness of skin barrier health and inflammation control, pointing to a more informed, preventative approach to skincare. Otherwise, the top-growing skincare brands in search data reflect a consumer preference for gentle, sensorial and results-oriented skincare with a global influence. Breeze Balm and Grace & Stella emphasise feel-good, pampering experiences, blending playful branding with functional hydration and glow-enhancing benefits.

On TikTok, trending beauty hashtags reveal that consumers are seeking long-lasting, performance-driven beauty solutions, as seen via #StayPutMakeup and #BlurringBlush. The emergence of #LashCleansing and #NourishingSkincare underscores a growing focus on gentle, supportive maintenance routines that prioritise skin and eye health alongside cosmetic use. #BridesmaidMakeupLook highlights a continued interest in occasion-based beauty inspiration, where consumers turn to social platforms for styling guidance tied to specific life events.

Recent findings suggest that the rise in search interest for products like hair loss cream, scalp serum, DHT blocker shampoo and flaky scalp shampoo reflects a pivot towards targeted, problem-solving haircare. Another recurring theme is scalp health, as consumers increasingly recognise that a healthy scalp underpins hair strength, therefore seeking solutions that address root causes like inflammation, build-up, or hormones. Functional plant-based ingredients (for example, onion for sulfur content), signal that shoppers are seeking nature-backed efficacy, or holistic benefits. Finally, the overlap in hair loss-related products (hair loss cream, DHT blockers) suggests a growing urgency around preventative care, especially among younger demographics looking to mitigate early signs of thinning or damage.

Trending haircare brands reflect a desire for elevated, wellness-infused beauty routines. Interest in Vichy’s dandruff shampoo and Umberto Giannini’s curl-focused products points to a demand for targeted solutions that address distinct scalp and textural needs. Rahua represents the appeal of botanical formulations rooted in sustainability, while Arey taps into age-conscious care with products designed to slow greying and support long-term hair vitality. Otherwise, the renewed buzz around Elizabeth and James’s now discontinued dry shampoo signals nostalgia-driven demand as well as the emotional value consumers place on high-performing staples.

This week, the fastest-growing TikTok hashtags point to a preference for practical, educational content that supports real-life beauty needs. Hashtags like #VacationSkincare and #FlawlessBaseRoutine reflect interest in context-specific routines that ensure skin confidence across different settings and occasions. Meanwhile, #HowToKnotlessBraid and #KbeautySkincareProducts show demand for culturally informed and technique-driven tutorials, underscoring the value placed on both inclusivity and precision. The popularity of #OatCleanser ties into the broader theme of gentle, skin-soothing ingredients, highlighting a shift towards mindful, barrier-friendly products.

This week, the popularity of gummies for creatine, ashwagandha, pre-workout and cortisol support indicates a desire for easy-to-integrate formats that make supplementation less clinical and more lifestyle friendly. The focus on adaptogens and hormonal balance (ashwagandha, cortisol supplements) signals heightened consumer interest in stress management and mental resilience, while tools like vibration plates align with a trend towards tech-enabled, at-home fitness enhancements. Together, these trends suggest a convergence of performance optimisation, stress relief and convenient wellness routines tailored to fast-paced lifestyles.

The top growing brands in the wellness space indicate that consumers are increasingly prioritising foundational health support, with a focus on targeted, bioavailable nutrients (for example, vitamins, minerals, electrolytes). Brands like Hiya Health and Ddrops reflect a shift towards family-focused and child-friendly wellness, suggesting rising parental investment in preventive health from an early age. The appeal of Cure Hydration and Bodyhealth points to interest in science-backed solutions for energy, recovery and hydration, often tied to active or wellness-conscious lifestyles.

According to recent reports, on beauty TikTok, the hashtags gaining the most traction reflect a demand for personalised, functional beauty routines rooted in real-life needs. #SPFMakeupProducts stands out as a clear signal of the rising interest in hybrid products that straddle skincare and cosmetics, showing that consumers want beauty items that offer both aesthetic and protective benefits, especially in terms of suncare. Hashtags like #FoundationFreeMakeup, #OilyHairProblems, #MyHairRoutine and #PerfumeJourney highlight minimalist beauty, relatable concerns and self-expression as key search themes through routine and scent, pointing to a desire for content that feels both aspirational and attainable.

In a recent development, trends in the bodycare space indicate a rising emphasis on functional selfcare that merges wellness with beauty. Products like magnesium oil and antibacterial soap bars reflect a demand for health-driven benefits, such as stress relief, muscle recovery and hygiene. Simultaneously, items like vanilla body scrub, exfoliating body lotion and moisture gloves show interest in sensorial indulgence and targeted skin treatments, pointing to a desire for multi-sensory and results-oriented routines. Overall, consumers are seeking efficacy and sensoriality in one, blending therapeutic ingredients with pleasurable experiences.

Sources indicate that among bodycare brands, there is a clear preference for intentional, streamlined routines that don’t sacrifice on quality or experience. Brands like Bend Soap Company and Noshinku lead with multifunctional, skin-friendly solutions that address sensitive skin and hygiene needs through nourishing, minimalist formats. Meanwhile, Head & Shoulders anchors the space with clinically proven performance, reinforcing the importance of efficacy alongside more indulgent or plant-based offerings.

Industry observers note that the beauty hashtags blowing up on TikTok this week reflect a consumer desire for creativity, inspiration and ritualised self-expression. #JumboLipBalm, sparked by Elf Cosmetics, showcases a playful, DIY spirit as customers recreate a viral product that blends nostalgia with beauty experimentation. #ColourfulEyeliner points to a growing appetite for bold, expressive looks, where makeup becomes a tool for individuality and artistic flair. #PromMakeupInspo and #HairWashingDay illustrate how special events and routine moments, respectively, are being transformed into meaningful, shareable rituals.
